papers.abstract: Ocean acidification, characterized by a gradual seawater pH decline, influences marine primary producers such as diatoms, which contribute substantially to oceanic carbon fixation. Experimental studies aiming to project climate change impacts often simulate acidification via abrupt pH shifts, potentially misrepresenting ecological and evolutionary responses. Here we conduct a long-term evolution experiment with the marine diatom Chaetoceros muelleri, comparing abrupt and gradual CO2 increases from 440 to 1000 ppm over 1100 generations. Integrating evolutionary genomics, physiological assays, elemental stoichiometry, and Earth System Modeling, we find that abrupt acidification exaggerates diatom growth and carbon fixation responses by up to 15%, driven by enhanced divergent genomic signals and persistent gene expression changes. Gradual acidification elicits weaker phenotypic and genomic shifts, aligning more closely with natural ocean conditions. These findings suggest that models based on abrupt CO2 increases may overestimate the contribution of Chaetoceros muelleri and maybe also other diatoms to productivity and biogeochemical cycling under ocean acidification, highlighting the importance of gradual pH decline in experimental designs to accurately predict marine ecosystem responses.

papers.abstract: Optical control of magnetization is often symmetry-forbidden because electric fields and magnetization transform differently under inversion and time-reversal. However, through even-order nonlinear response, optical excitation can generate a nonequilibrium magnetic density (the nonlinear Edelstein effect) that acts as an internal Edelstein-Zeeman field coupling to slower magnetic degrees of freedom. Here we demonstrate non-thermal, ultrafast optical control of ferromagnetism in the centrosymmetric van der Waals semiconductor Cr2Ge2Te6 via a resonant nonlinear Edelstein effect. Using time-domain THz emission spectroscopy under near-infrared excitation, we directly observe magnetic dipole radiation arising from optically driven magnetization dynamics. The polarization, fluence, and temperature dependences of the THz emission are quantitatively captured by a mean-field description of a weakly anisotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet subject to an Edelstein-Zeeman field. Our results establish a general nonequilibrium route to optical control of magnetism in centrosymmetric materials.

papers.abstract: Despite progress on noble-metal high-entropy alloy catalysts, noble-metal-free high-entropy alloy catalysts continue to face limitations in activity and stability. Atomic defect engineering holds promise for unlocking catalytic potential, yet efficient strategies for designing defects to simultaneously tailor electronic structures and enhance catalytic active sites in noble-metal-free high-entropy alloys remain challenging. Here, we report a general rule to drive twin formation via precisely tuning lattice strain in metallic nanomaterials. By modeling twin formation energy as a descriptor and employing a gradient-radius hetero-atomic doping strategy, we derive a generalized lattice strain-twin formation energy function that determines critical strain for twinning propensity. Guided by this principle, Ce is incorporated into CuCoNiMnMo nanoparticles, promoting coherent five-fold twinning along {111} planes. Twin boundaries generate high-activity sites by disrupting atomic symmetry and reducing coordination numbers, while modulating band width via altered orbital overlap. Meanwhile, strong Ce-O affinity forms an amorphous CeOx passivation layer on twinned noble-metal-free high-entropy alloy, triggering hetero-interfacial electron transfer. These effects synergistically optimize reaction kinetics. Consequently, the engineered catalyst achieves a 405-cycle lifespan in lithium-oxygen batteries and operates across -20 to 80 °C. Our study brings fundamental insights into defect engineering for electrocatalysis in energy conversion fields.

papers.abstract: Learning to link sensory information to motor actions requires coordinated activity across the cerebral cortex, but how different cortical layers contribute to learning remains unclear. Here we show that learning engages distinct, layer-specific activity patterns across the cortex of male mice during acquisition of a whisker-based go/no-go task. Using wide-field calcium imaging of either layer 2/3 or layer 5 neurons across 25 cortical areas, we found that learning produced markedly different, and sometimes opposing, changes in activity between layers. Layer 5 exhibited widespread suppression before sensory input and enhanced activity in frontal cortex during sensorimotor transformation, whereas layer 2/3 showed learning-related enhancements in higher-order sensory areas during sensation. In contrast, both layers displayed similar learning-related enhancement in barrel cortex during whisker touch. These findings reveal complementary roles of superficial and deep cortical layers during learning and demonstrate that layer-specific cortical dynamics are a fundamental feature of sensorimotor learning.

papers.abstract: Diet is associated with biological aging, yet few existing dietary indices have been developed specifically to target biological aging. We develop a data-driven, food-based Empirical Dietary Index for Slower Epigenetic Aging (EDISEA) to identify dietary features predictive of lower GrimAge2 acceleration. Higher EDISEA is associated with 4.17 years slower epigenetic aging in the derivation sample of 1,711 participants (P-value < 0.001) and 3.77 years slower aging in an independent sample of 2,311 participants. Higher EDISEA is consistently associated with lower all-cause mortality (pooled hazard ratio = 0.80, 95% CI 0.76, 0.85) in two US cohorts, and with lower risks of aging-related diseases, functional limitations, and multimorbidity across US and UK aging cohorts. Outcome-wide analyses in a large UK population-based cohort further show broad health associations, supported by molecular and neuroimaging signatures of more favourable vascular, inflammatory, metabolic, and brain structural profiles. EDISEA may provide an epigenetic aging-informed framework for studying dietary strategies relevant to healthy aging.

papers.abstract: Phosphorylation plays a central role in coordinating transcription with pre-mRNA maturation, yet the mechanistic understanding of how transcription is regulated by phosphorylation remains limited. The PP1 phosphatase removes Cdk9-dependent phosphorylation of Pol II and Spt5, triggering transcription termination. Here, we demonstrate that PNUTS enhances PP1 activity, whereas WDR82 mediates an interaction between PP1 and the pre-mRNA 3'-end processing machinery subunit Symplekin. We present the structure of a PNUTS-WDR82-Symplekin-Ssu72 complex, revealing that PNUTS and Symplekin bind WDR82 through distinct interfaces using conserved short linear motifs. Mutations that inactivate PP1's catalytic activity or disrupt its interaction with either PNUTS or the 3'-end processing machinery led to impaired transcription elongation, inefficient cleavage of nascent transcripts, altered poly(A) site selection, and widespread transcription termination defects. Our findings demonstrate that the PP1 complex is essential for coupling transcription to pre-mRNA 3'-end maturation, ensuring production of functional mRNA.

papers.abstract: Aerogel fibers have many advantages for personal thermal management because of their three-dimensional porous structures, high porosity, thermal insulation, and effective passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) capabilities. However, the porous structure of aerogel fibers significantly weakens their mechanical strength, thereby reducing their cooling efficiency. Here, we develop a method for the continuous production of radially gradient porous bacterial cellulose (BC) aerogel fibers (GP-BCAFs) fabrics. The multilevel gradient micro- and nano-porous structures of the GP-BCAFs provide a high solar reflectivity, while the nano-entangled networks and distinctive wrinkled pores improve their mechanical properties by dissipating stress. The designed structure achieves a balance between strong mechanical properties and cooling performance. The GP-BCAF fabrics exhibit a high mechanical and PDRC performance, including a tensile strength of 50 MPa, a solar reflectivity of 94.7%, a mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity of 97.3%, and an outdoor cooling performance with 8.5 °C temperature lower than that of commercial cotton fabrics. Moreover, a self-powered sensor is built using the GP-BCAF fabric, and its electrical signals allow real-time monitoring of human physiological activities. This work provides a universal, sustainable, and scalable approach to producing PDRC aerogel fibers and multifunctional textiles for outdoor personal thermal management.

papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

papers.abstract: While microglia are well known for pruning synapses during neurodevelopment, their role in synapse formation remains understudied. Here we investigate how microglial absence impacts synaptic development in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), a region critical for emotional regulation and motivated behaviors. Using genetically modified mice lacking microglia (Csf1rΔFIRE/ΔFIRE), we find blunted excitatory synapse formation in the NAc, particularly during the second and third postnatal weeks. Tissue-level NAc proteomics in the third postnatal week reveals changes in proteins involved in synapse structure, trans-synaptic signaling, and pre-synaptic function. Although electrophysiological changes largely resolve by adulthood, microglia-lacking mice exhibit persistent changes in threat avoidance behavior and underlying NAc neuronal activity. Transient depletion of NAc microglia during the second postnatal week similarly disrupts synapse formation and adult threat avoidance. Together, these findings identify a role for microglia in shaping NAc synaptic development and in establishing functional circuits that support adult behavioral function.

papers.abstract: With the miniaturization and high integration of microelectronic devices, efficient thermal management is increasingly critical. Conventional thermal interface materials often suffer from a certain degree of mismatch between their thermal conductivity and contact thermal resistance. Herein, we develop a thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel with a branched-type nanocluster-junction network. Benefiting from the interfacial infiltration enabled by the branched-junction fluoronetwork and the efficient thermal pathways constructed by thermal conductive nanocomposites, the fluorofluidic-gel exhibits a high thermal conductivity of 5.89 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ and a low contact thermal resistance of 0.15 cm²·K·W⁻¹. It also achieves reversible adhesion and mechanical resistance, with an adhesive strength of 189.3 kPa, adhesion energy of 220.3 J·m⁻² and impact resistance of 3.91 J·cm⁻¹. In addition, this gel maintains thermal stability from -80 °C to 300 °C and exhibits an electrical breakdown strength exceeding 24 kV/mm. We ‌anticipate‌ that adaptive thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel presents a promising solution for high-heat-flux electronic thermal management.

papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections are a global threat, yet their long-term pathogen-specific mortality dynamics and pandemic-era deviations remain unclear. In this secondary modelling analysis, we evaluate associated mortality under a no-infection counterfactual and attributable mortality under a drug-susceptible infection counterfactual for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections overall and across seven constituent pathogen groups in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Using age-period-cohort decomposition and Bayesian counterfactual modelling, we estimate 1.03 million associated (95% uncertainty interval, 0.90-1.17 million) and 0.22 million attributable (0.17-0.27 million) deaths from these infections in 2021. From 1990 to 2019, overall associated and attributable mortality rates increased by 0.82% (95% confidence interval, 0.77-0.87) and 0.90% (0.85-0.95) per year, respectively. South Asia has the fastest-rising associated and attributable mortality, whereas high-income regions decline. Among constituent pathogens, Klebsiella pneumoniae shows the fastest increase in mortality rates, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa shows declining associated but slightly rising attributable mortality. During 2020-2021, overall associated mortality falls 4.71% below pre-pandemic counterfactual projections, whereas attributable mortality does not change significantly. Here, we show divergent mortality trajectories by region, pathogen, and metric, motivating targeted, dual-metric surveillance and intervention strategies.

papers.title: Global spatiotemporal dynamics of mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections over the past three decades.

papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Here, we perform genomic and structural analyses of 44 BDBV sequences, including 12 from the 2026 outbreak, to assess mAb binding to the viral glycoprotein (GP). While the MBP134 cocktail epitopes remain conserved, mAb114 (Ebanga) binding is compromised by E112D and P116A mutations, causing off-target binding and reduced affinity. Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. These computational models predict mAb114 efficacy against BDBV may be compromised due to epitope mutations affecting binding affinity, whereas MBP134 retains conserved targeting and holds promise as a broadly protective therapeutic. The complex binding behavior of Inmazeb components points to the importance of antibody combinatorial effects for treatment efficacy. These observations warrant urgent experimental validation through neutralization assays.

papers.abstract: Understanding tissue function requires connecting spatial cellular context with molecular depth, yet such integration remains challenging in complex organs like the pancreas. We develop multiplexed Deep Visual Proteomics (mxDVP), an end-to-end workflow combining high-plex imaging, automated computational analysis, and spatially guided ultra-sensitive mass spectrometry. Powered by PIPΣX, an open-source image analysis framework enabling whole-slide membrane-aware segmentation, annotation, and laser microdissection export, mxDVP achieves >6000 protein identifications from as few as 100 small islet cells. Applied to human pancreatic islets, mxDVP segments over 860,000 cells and resolves twelve endocrine subtypes, including rare polyhormonal and intermediate-state populations that exhibit spatial organization patterns, co-expression of INSM1 and SCG3, and hybrid α/β/δ signatures. These findings reveal a spectrum of endocrine heterogeneity and spatial organization. By integrating imaging and deep proteomics in an accessible framework, mxDVP enables discovery of rare cell states whose biological roles depend on tissue architecture.

papers.abstract: Integrating sensing into communication is crucial for the fully-connected and intelligent development of modern life. However, existing fiber-optic sensing and communication systems merely coexist without inadequate resource sharing, resulting in limited scalability for large-scale deployment. Here, we propose a holistically co-designed sensing and communication (CSAC) framework that incorporates multi-level optimization: (i) a dual-function pilot signal that shares time and spectrum resources; (ii) a simplified system using a single transmitter to simultaneously generate multi-tone pilot and subcarrier communication signals; (iii) a point-to-multipoint (P2MP) network that distributes pilot signals for multi-user frequency synchronization and enhanced acoustic sensing response. Our approach achieves multi-point frequency synchronization with an accuracy of 1.56 MHz and enhances acoustic sensing response to 12 kHz. By introducing the on-chip modulators to generate multi-frequency optical comb, the response bandwidth is further expanded to 28 kHz. This CSAC framework efficiently supports dense communication and diverse sensing, offering an eco-sustainable solution for the future optical networks.

papers.abstract: For advanced EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKI) therapy is the primary treatment, but drug resistance and side effects reduce its effectiveness. Integrating Chinese and Western medicine is a key focus in cancer treatment. This study evaluates the clinical benefits of combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with EGFR-TKI, summarizing TCM syndromes and medication traits. We searched six databases for relevant clinical studies. A meta-analysis assessed progression-free survival (PFS), disease control rate (DCR), and adverse reactions, with subgroup analysis by EGFR mutation type. A TCM syndrome network was created to examine syndrome distribution and core prescription patterns. TCM combined with EGFR-TKIs significantly improved PFS (HR = 0.70, 95%CI 0.65-0.76, p < 0.00001, I² = 0%), benefiting patients with Exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation equally (p = 0.75). The combination therapy increased DCR (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.01-1.40, p = 0.04), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 89%), and reduced targeted-agent-related adverse reactions. Qi-Yin and Lung-Spleen deficiency were the dominant TCM syndromes, managed via Qi-tonifying, Yin-nourishing and spleen-strengthening regimens. Integrating TCM with EGFR-TKI enhances tumor control and treatment safety in advanced NSCLC patients with EGFR mutations, showing consistent efficacy across various mutation types. This approach, which considers clinical syndrome differentiation and medication patterns in Chinese medicine, offers evidence-based guidance for personalized treatment. This review was performed following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398486, identifier CRD420261398486.

papers.abstract: The introduction of volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) has enabled dosimetric improvements during prostate bed (PB) radiotherapy; however, the planning target volume (PTV) margins remain substantially greater than for prostate radiotherapy. New approaches are required to further optimise rectal dose and minimise target and organ motion. ProSpare®, a self-inserted rectal obturator designed to facilitate daily image guidance, may enhance radiotherapy accuracy and reduce treatment-related morbidity. Patients scheduled to receive adjuvant or salvage PB radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy were randomised to either standard-of-care (SOC) PB-IMRT using centre-standard PTV margins and verification protocol (SOC) or PB-IMRT with daily ProSpare®-guided radiotherapy using a reduced 5-mm posterior margin. Dose and fractionation schedules were selected by each centre according to protocol recommendations. The primary endpoint is patient-reported EPIC bowel function and bother at 2 years. Secondary endpoints include acute Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) and CTCAE toxicity, patient-reported outcomes, device tolerability, and anorectal dosimetry. We report the results from the prespecified analysis of these secondary endpoints. Between 2017 and 2023, 162 patients were recruited; 158 began radiotherapy and were evaluable at 18 weeks. Acute toxicity data were available for 146 patients (SOC 76/81, ProSpare 70/77). Compared with SOC, ProSpare® was associated with lower 18-week RTOG ≥grade 1 gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) toxicity (39% vs. 31% and 37% vs. 29%, respectively). The incidence of worst CTCAE grade 2 GI and GU toxicity was <6%. Of 51 responders, 50 found ProSpare® tolerable and would recommend its use. Use of ProSpare® resulted in consistently lower ano-rectal dose-volume parameters. ProSpare®-guided prostate bed radiotherapy (PBRT) resulted in lower acute RTOG bowel toxicity at all time points. Patient-reported tolerability was very favourable. Use of ProSpare® improved rectal and anal canal dosimetry. ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT02978014.

papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and most patients present with unresectable or metastatic disease. In recent years, approaches such as locoregional therapy, immunotherapy and targeted therapy have achieved significant breakthroughs in the transformation treatment of advanced iCCA. We report a case of successful conversion therapy using envafolimab plus olaparib combined with locoregional therapies in advanced iCCA. A 65-year-old male with obstructive jaundice was diagnosed with metastatic iCCA (cT3N1M1, Stage IV) harboring a 117 mm left hepatic lobe lesion, with enlarged lymph nodes, and pulmonary nodules suspicious for metastasis. Next-generation sequencing revealed MSI-H and TMB-H status, along with DDR gene alterations (CDK12 and HDAC2). He received multimodal treatment comprising TACE, HAIC, PD-L1 blockade (envafolimab), and exploratory PARP inhibition (olaparib). Over 20 months, the primary lesion shrank from 117 mm to 42 mm, with regression of lymph nodules and pulmonary nodules and normalization of CA19-9. He underwent R0 resection and pathological examination confirmed a pathological complete response (pCR/ypT0N0) in the resected specimens. At the last follow-up (October 15, 2025), the patient had achieved a progression-free survival of 36 months and a postoperative recurrence-free survival of 16 months. This case demonstrates that the TACE plus HAIC combined with PD-L1 blockade and exploratory PARP inhibition is a promising conversion therapy strategy. It provides preliminary evidence for PARP inhibitor therapy in DDR-altered cholangiocarcinoma, supporting further investigation in prospective trials.

papers.abstract: Previous studies have identified an association between a tumor microenvironment characterized by a predominance of T helper cell type 2 (Th2) system cells (Th2 cells, M2 macrophages, innate lymphoid cells type 2), regulatory T cells, and myeloid derived suppressor cells with poorer cancer prognosis. In contrast, a tumor microenvironment characterized by Th1 system cells (Th1 cells, M1 macrophages, natural killer cells, CD8+ cells, innate lymphoid cells type 1) is associated with a more favorable prognosis. T2-high asthma, a quintessential Th2-dominance-based disease, is associated epidemiologically with more than double the incidence of lung, breast, prostate, and colon cancers, suggesting a connection between the Th2 immune dominant patient macroenvironment and the Th2 immune dominant tumor microenvironment. Stress, air pollution, toxicants, sleep disruption, obesity, and many other influences from the exposome are known to drive the patient into Th2 dominance. Thus, the authors hypothesize that there is a through-line connecting the exposome, patient macroenvironment, and tumor microenvironment. With this context in mind, specific defects in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle produce oncometabolites that drive oncogenic development in tissues. However these same TCA cycle defects drive macrophages to the M1 phenotype, which activates the Th1 system. Th1 system cells are responsible for clearance of oncogenically transformed cells. This should represent a check against the oncogenic influence of the oncometabolites created by the TCA cycle breaks. The authors hypothesize that, in Th2 dominant patients, the TCA cycle breaks fail to shift macrophages to the M1 phenotype, the Th1 system fails to upregulate, and the normal check against oncogenic development fails to occur. If confirmed by subsequent studies, this model may help explain the more than doubled incidence of common cancers in asthma and potentially other Th2 atopic diseases. The authors discuss clinical implications and approaches for operationalizing existing knowledge of the exposome and its impact on patient immunology.

papers.title: Influencing the exposome, patient macroenvironment, tumor microenvironment through-line to improve clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Colorectal adenomas (CRAs) are the primary precancerous lesions in the development of colorectal cancer; establishing a simple, cost-effective and non-invasive tool for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy is of great significance for risk stratification. To investigate the association between peripheral blood metabolic and inflammatory markers and the risk of colorectal adenomas, and to develop a personalised risk prediction model for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy. This study was a single-centre retrospective case-control study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong Second Medical University. The study included 2,437 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent endoscopic resection between January 2020 and December 2025. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors and peripheral blood biochemical markers, with a particular focus on the triglyceride-to-glucose (TyG) ratio and markers of systemic inflammation. Patients with colorectal adenomas confirmed by histopathology. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The study included 2,437 participants (mean age 58.57 years; 1,323 men [54.29%]), patients in the adenoma group (n=1,584) were significantly older and had a higher proportion of men compared with the control group (n=853). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that male sex (OR, 1.621; 95% CI, 1.269-2.074), age ≥56.5 years (OR, 1.868; 95% CI, 1.515-2.205) and a TyG index ≥8.562 (OR, 1.271; 95% CI, 1.015-1.590) were independent risk factors for the development of colorectal adenomas. The AUC of this predictive model was 0.631 and 0.607 in the training and validation sets, respectively, indicates moderate discriminatory power. The model is well calibrated; analysis of the decision curve shows that, across a range of threshold probabilities, the model yields a positive net benefit compared with strategies involving either universal treatment or universal non-treatment. The findings suggest that male gender, advanced age and an elevated TyG index are independently associated with the risk of colorectal adenomas. The non-invasive nomogram developed in this study provides a simple risk stratification tool to aid in distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy.

papers.title: Risk factors associated with colorectal adenomas and the formulation of prediction models.

papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent extracranial solid malignant tumor in infants and children. Approximately half of children with high-risk NB exhibit primary resistance to first-line therapy or experience disease relapse within two years post-treatment, leading to dismal overall survival. PANoptosis is an inflammatory programmed cell death modality integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis; nevertheless, the functional relevance of PANoptosis-related genes (PRGs) in NB remains largely undefined. This study aimed to explore PRGs associated with NB prognosis and their link to the tumor immune microenvironment, so as to identify novel therapeutic targets for NB. mRNA expression profiles from three public NB datasets (GSE49711-NB, TARGET-NB and E-MTAB-8248-NB) were used to investigate the prognostic roles of 19 previously reported PRGs. Independent Cox regression screening was performed in each cohort to identify cohort-specific prognostic PRGs, followed by Venn intersection analysis to identify conserved prognostic genes. PARP1 expression was validated in tumor tissues from 127 clinical NB patients. The GIS score based on PARP1 expression and clinical metadata were combined to assess its prognostic value. In vitro functional assays were performed to explore the anti-tumor effects and mechanisms of the PARP1 inhibitor AZD5305. Venn intersection analysis identified PARP1 as the only shared gene with consistent prognostic significance across heterogeneous NB patient populations. In vitro experiments revealed that AZD5305 markedly suppressed NB cell proliferation, migration and invasion, triggered cell apoptosis, and arrested cell cycle progression at the G0/G1 phase. This study adopts a multi-cohort parallel screening strategy to mine conserved therapeutic targets for NB. Our data indicate that PARP1 inhibition via AZD5305 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for NB treatment.

papers.abstract: This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

papers.abstract: Obesity increases the risk and progression of at least 13 types of cancer. Although the epidemiologic links between excess adiposity and these cancers are well documented, the biological mechanisms linking obesity to carcinogenesis and tumor progression remain incompletely understood. White adipose tissue in obesity is a source of inflammatory and immunosuppressive signals that act systemically, driving metabolic, inflammatory, and immune dysfunction whose consequences differ across tumor types. As adipose tissue expands and adipocytes enlarge, the blood supply becomes inadequate, leading to hypoxia, fibrosis, lipolytic stress, macrophage recruitment, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These obesity-induced perturbations generate endocrine, cytokine, lipid, and metabolic signals that act systemically, within the tumor microenvironment (TME), and/or cell-intrinsically to activate oncogenic and tumor-promoting pathways. The same signals reshape innate and adaptive immunity, promoting tumor-permissive macrophage states and myeloid-derived suppressor cell expansion, while the effector arms weaken as antigen presentation, natural killer cell and T cell function all decline. This review synthesizes current evidence linking obesity-associated inflammation and immune dysregulation to cancer initiation, progression, and treatment responses across multiple obesity-related cancers. Emphasis is placed on adipose tissue inflammation, myeloid cell biology, T cell immunometabolism, endocrine-inflammatory crosstalk, and the relationship between obesity and immunotherapy. Finally, we discuss translational opportunities for preventing or intercepting obesity-related cancers, including weight loss achieved through lifestyle, surgical, or pharmacologic approaches, with an emphasis on GLP-1 receptor agonists given their substantial efficacy, rapid clinical uptake, and potential to reshape obesity-related cancer prevention and survivorship strategies. Defining the metabolic, immune, and inflammatory phenotypes that drive obesity-associated cancer risk and progression will be essential for developing more precise, mechanism-based strategies for prevention, treatment, and survivorship care.

papers.abstract: Engineered microbial immunotherapies can localize immune-modulating signals within solid tumors, where hypoxia, suppressive myeloid cells, deficient antigen presentation, and dysfunctional T-cell trafficking often limit immunotherapy. Macrofungal polysaccharides, especially structurally defined β-glucans, offer mechanistic templates rather than interchangeable drug substances for source-specific, structure-controlled immune engineering programs. Their activity depends on linkage, branching, molecular mass, conformation, solubility, aggregation, and physical presentation. Critically, the strongest Dectin-1 and trained-immunity evidence discussed here uses particulate β-glucans from Saccharomyces cerevisiae; those findings cannot be assigned directly to macrofungal β-glucans without material-specific comparison. We therefore distinguish four engineering architectures: de novo microbial biosynthesis of a defined β-glucan, microbial surface display, delivery of a pre-characterized β-glucan cargo, and delivery of non-glycan payloads that mimic the desired downstream immune program. Because therapeutic bacteria have not yet been shown to reproduce a macrofungal β-glucan with controlled linkage, branching, conformation, and presentation, near-term development should prioritize standardized cargo delivery or pathway mimicry. In pancreatic and colorectal cancer models, yeast whole-glucan particles have altered myeloid trafficking or generated epigenetically and metabolically trained macrophages linked to CXCL9/CXCL10 production, natural killer-cell recruitment, conventional type 1 dendritic-cell accumulation, and stronger CD8 T-cell responses. Human evidence remains preliminary and cannot establish β-glucan-specific efficacy in uncontrolled combination studies. This Perspective proposes source-resolved material characterization, receptor and cell-state testing, multidimensional pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and microbial safety controls as prerequisites for translating fungal-inspired immune programs into precision cancer therapeutics.

papers.abstract: Clinically node-negative (cN0) breast cancer accounts for a large proportion of newly diagnosed cases, and its axillary management is undergoing a paradigm shift toward de-escalation aimed at minimizing surgical morbidity. Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) has replaced axillary lymph node dissection (ALND) for nodal staging in cN0 disease, and subsequent trials have questioned the need for completion ALND in selected SLN-positive patients. This narrative review summarizes two decades of pivotal trial evidence across three conceptually distinct de-escalation strategies, which differ in their levels of evidence. First, phase III randomized evidence supports omission of ALND after a positive SLNB for isolated tumor cells and micrometastases (IBCSG 23-01; 10-year disease-free survival HR 0.85, with the non-inferiority criterion met), and for 1-2 macrometastases when combined with breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy (ACOSOG Z0011, AMAROS, SENOMAC). Second, omission of SLNB itself has demonstrated 5-year oncological safety in rigorously selected low-risk patients with small tumors and negative preoperative axillary ultrasonography (SOUND, INSEMA), in cohorts that were predominantly HR-positive/HER2-negative. Third, emerging strategies, such as advanced imaging, ctDNA-based monitoring, and AI-assisted diagnostics, may further refine patient selection but remain investigational and are not part of established clinical practice at present. The current evidence is insufficient to support routine de-escalation in HER2-positive and triple-negative disease or in other populations underrepresented in the pivotal trials. Axillary de-escalation is therefore justified only within the specific clinical scenarios validated by randomized trials, and aggressive subtypes and biomarker-guided strategies require further prospective evidence before integration into clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Background: In Ghana, prostate cancer (PCa) was the second most frequently diagnosed cancer among men in 2022, after liver cancer. Despite increasing research interest, evidence needed to guide PCa research priorities remains fragmented. This scoping review aimed to highlight research priorities and direction on PCa in Ghana by identifying thematic areas, gaps and potential areas for future research. Methods: The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews checklist (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search for relevant articles was conducted on four prominent databases: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ScienceDirect. Results: Data from eligible studies (n = 47) were synthesized across 15 thematic domains, including awareness, diagnosis and treatment approaches, genetics, dietary and metabolic factors, and pharmacological interventions. PCa awareness was high in some populations, but knowledge of specific disease features was variable, while screening uptake remained low. PSA was the most frequently assessed diagnostic marker, commonly evaluated alongside DRE and biopsy. Genomic studies identified potentially relevant genetic and molecular variants, although the evidence remains limited and requires further validation. Treatment patterns varied by disease stage and were also constrained by access- and resource-related factors. Epidemiological estimates differed by study design and population. Conclusions: PCa research in Ghana is broad but uneven, with significant gaps in early detection, population-level data, genomic validation and equitable access to care. Improving timely diagnosis and access to diagnostic and treatment services is important, while population-wide screening requires further evaluation of benefits, harms, cost-effectiveness, and health system capacity.

papers.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of multimodal hyperspectral spectroscopy (MHS) using the LuViva® Advanced Cervical Scan for the detection of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) in women referred for further cervical assessment. Methods: This prospective, non-randomized diagnostic study included 77 women examined between September 2025 and April 2026. Participants were referred because of abnormal liquid-based cytology (LBC), high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, or other indications for colposcopy. LuViva examination was performed before colposcopy with cervical biopsy. Histopathological diagnosis based on biopsy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure specimens was used as the reference standard. The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy were calculated for HR-HPV testing, LBC, and different LuViva positivity thresholds. Results: The mean age was 39.0 ± 8.4 years. The final histopathology showed no lesions in 30 women, LSIL in 18, HSIL in 28, and cervical cancer in one. For CIN2+ detection, HR-HPV testing demonstrated a sensitivity of 93.1% and specificity of 29.2%, whereas LBC had a sensitivity of 82.8% and specificity of 39.6%. LuViva testing showed sensitivities between 82.8% and 100%, and a specificity-when comparing with LBC-of 45.8% but 20.8% in LuViva alone. LuViva results differ significantly between women with CIN2+ and those with LSIL or no lesions. Conclusions: LuViva showed potential as an adjunctive triage tool, as no CIN2+ lesions were observed among women with a low-risk result; however, the small number of negative tests and wide confidence intervals preclude safely deferring colposcopy. The AND strategy showed a modest numerical improvement in specificity and overall accuracy compared with LBC alone but did not show an increase in sensitivity; this finding should be considered exploratory.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now applied across the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) pathway, yet the literature has grown faster than the evidence needed to act on it. The question is not whether an algorithm can predict an endpoint, but whether it yields information reliable, generalizable, and actionable enough to change a clinically meaningful decision. In this narrative, in a non-systematic review of PDAC-specific literature, we grade applications on an author-defined evidence-readiness framework (development, internal, external, prospective validation, clinical impact, and implementation) and on four dimensions-validation, comparator, actionability, and impact. Contemporary meta-analyses show high pooled accuracy for AI-based early detection and for distinguishing PDAC from mass-forming pancreatitis (sensitivity ~0.88-0.92, specificity ~0.90-0.93), but with extreme heterogeneity, low radiomics quality, scarce external validation, and-for electronic health-record risk models-positive predictive values often below 1% at population prevalence. Computed tomography (CT)-based detection and risk enrichment are among the more mature applications identified, yet none has been shown to improve stage distribution, resection rate, or survival. Treatment prediction is held to a strict standard, distinguishing prognostic association from a validated treatment-by-biomarker interaction. The rate-limiting steps are no longer algorithmic but translational-external and prospective validation, calibration, appropriate comparators, and workflow integration.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of relapsed or refractory hematological malignancies, producing deep and durable responses in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas, and multiple myeloma. Nevertheless, antigen escape, limited in vivo persistence, T-cell exhaustion, and toxicities such as cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) limit broader application. This review synthesizes the mechanistic basis and clinical evidence for the currently approved CAR T-cell products and examines engineering strategies designed to overcome these barriers, including "armored" CAR T cells, multitargeted and logic-gated constructs, and modular or universal platforms intended to extend this approach beyond CD19-positive disease. Combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors, radiotherapy, and other immunotherapies are discussed, together with emerging biomarkers of response and toxicity. Continued optimization of CAR design, toxicity management, and manufacturing scalability will be essential for CAR T-cell therapy to become a foundational pillar of precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Background: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a complex malignancy, and the molecular mechanisms that drive its progression have not yet been fully elucidated. Eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E (eIF4E), a pivotal regulator of protein synthesis, is frequently dysregulated in cancers. We previously identified eIF4E as a direct transcriptional target of Yin Yang 1 (YY1) in an axis where YY1 suppressed NPC invasion and metastasis. Methods: Here, we investigated the function of eIF4E in NPC growth and its regulatory relationship with YY1. The CCK-8 assay, clonogenic survival assay, Annexin V/propidium iodide assay, and xenograft models were used to determine the role of YY1/eIF4E in NPC growth; Western blotting and Co-IP were performed to examine protein expression and protein-protein interactions, respectively. Results: Our findings demonstrate that eIF4E potently promoted NPC cell proliferation, accelerated cell cycle progression, and inhibited apoptosis. Moreover, these effects were critically dependent on its phosphorylation at serine 209 (S209). Furthermore, we uncovered a novel regulatory mechanism whereby YY1 enhances the association between 4E-BP1 and eIF4E, downregulates eIF4G expression, and is associated with reduced interaction between eIF4E and eIF4G, thereby potentially limiting eIF4F complex formation. Conclusions: This study establishes eIF4E phosphorylation as an oncogenic driver of NPC cell growth and survival and identifies YY1 as a tumor suppressor that negatively regulates this axis. These insights position eIF4E as a promising and precise therapeutic target for NPC intervention.

papers.abstract: Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the predominant type of liver cancer, exhibits a high mortality rate due to unclear molecular mechanisms and limited biomarkers. Accumulating evidence indicates that splicing factors (SFs) can promote tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance by altering the splicing patterns of target genes. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying SF-mediated alternative splicing (AS) are highly intricate, and the specific functions and pathways of SFs in HCC initiation and progression remain to be further elucidated. Methods: First, Cox regression and LASSO regression analyses of splicing factors (SFs) were performed using the TCGA database, followed by validation using the ICGC dataset. The prognostic value of SFPQ was assessed with the Kaplan-Meier plotter. Next, the potential association of SFPQ with the immune microenvironment of HCC was explored using TIMER and CIBERSORT. In addition, we screened AS events associated with SFPQ expression in TCGA-LIHC, conducted GO/KEGG pathway enrichment analyses, and investigated the correlation between GTF2H3 percent spliced in index (PSI) values and clinicopathological features in HCC patients. Finally, the effect of targeting the exon 10- or exon 11-containing variants of GTF2H3 on HCC was examined at the cellular level. Results: LASSO regression analysis identified five key SFs significantly associated with HCC prognosis, including SFPQ, HTRA2, DAZAP1, PCBP2, and YBX1. Among these, SFPQ was determined as the most critical SF influencing HCC survival, and its overexpression was positively correlated with HCC progression. GO and KEGG analyses revealed that the pathways potentially associated with SFPQ include metabolic pathways, oxidative phosphorylation, mRNA surveillance pathway, and the PPAR signaling pathway. Furthermore, SFPQ expression was associated with the exclusion of exons 10 and 11 of the GTF2H3 gene. Computational analysis also suggested a potential link between SFPQ and immune cell infiltration. Targeting the exon 11-containing variant of GTF2H3 significantly reduced cell viability and migration of HCC cells. Conclusion: SFPQ expression is elevated in HCC and correlates with tumor aggressiveness and poor patient prognosis. Our findings suggest that SFPQ may influence HCC progression through its association with the GTF2H3 exon 10/11 ME event and the immune microenvironment. However, further experimental validation is required to confirm these mechanisms. Our findings suggest that SFPQ may serve as a promising biomarker and therapeutic candidate for HCC.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adult-type diffuse gliomas (ADGs) are aggressive brain tumors with highly variable clinical outcomes. Prognostic assessment directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) could support personalized decision-making. Methods: To our knowledge, this is the first systematic benchmarking of pathology foundation models (FMs) and multiple instance learning (MIL) methods for overall survival (OS) risk stratification in ADGs under the 2021 World Health Organization (WHO) classification. A retrospective, multi-institutional cohort of 817 subjects from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) was analyzed. Following tissue segmentation and patch-level curation, we evaluated 77 pathology FM-MIL combinations (11 FMs × 7 MIL methods), together with seven ResNet-50 baseline configurations (84 encoder-MIL configurations in total), using patient-level 10-fold cross-validation. A perturbation-based evaluation assessed attention mechanism faithfulness. Results: UNI2 paired with MambaMIL achieved the highest cross-validated concordance index (C-index = 0.77), whereas its time-dependent AUC was modest (0.60-0.61 at 12-36 months), and several combinations performed comparably. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant separation between high- and low-risk groups (log-rank p = 9.16 × 10-17; hazard ratio [HR] = 2.90, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.23-3.76), with a median OS of 16.6 months (95% CI: 15.0-20.4) versus 63.5 months (95% CI: 43.9-NR), respectively. Tertile stratification confirmed a monotonic OS gradient from 94.5 months to 14.7 months (p = 3.25 × 10-17). Risk stratification within individual WHO 2021 types was not significant. Most domain-specific FMs outperformed the ImageNet-pretrained baseline, and the removal of highly attended patches reduced performance, supporting attention faithfulness. Conclusions: The AI-derived risk score remained associated with OS after adjustment for individual clinical and molecular variables, but independent prognostic value was not demonstrated in the fully adjusted model (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: 0.94-1.85, p = 0.104), and its discrimination largely reflects differences between WHO 2021 types. This benchmarking framework provides guidance for FM-MIL design in computational pathology applications targeting survival prediction; external validation is required before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Background: Cardiotoxicity remains a major limitation of contemporary cancer therapies, affecting morbidity and long-term outcomes among cancer survivors. Early identification of patients at increased cardiovascular risk is essential to guide surveillance and preventive strategies. Methods and Results: We performed a narrative review of currently available risk assessment and prediction approaches for cancer therapy-related cardiotoxicity, including consensus-based frameworks, statistically derived prediction models, and emerging machine learning-based approaches. Widely used tools, such as the HFA-ICOS (Heart Failure Association-International Cardio-Oncology Society) risk assessment framework, provide a practical and standardized approach to baseline risk stratification and are increasingly implemented in clinical practice. However, their discriminative performance appears variable across studies, and their applicability across diverse oncologic populations may be limited. Key challenges include heterogeneity in cardiotoxicity definitions, limited external validation, and incomplete integration of dynamic parameters. Overall, models based primarily on clinical variables demonstrate only moderate predictive accuracy, particularly in patients receiving anthracyclines. Conclusions: Current risk stratification strategies provide a useful foundation for clinical decision-making but remain limited in their ability to fully capture individual risk. Future approaches should integrate clinical variables with circulating biomarkers, advanced imaging, and AI to enable more dynamic and individualized risk prediction in cardio-oncology.

papers.abstract: The use of targeted therapies in oncology has increased significantly, but associated cutaneous adverse events often impair quality of life and adherence. Despite numerous available interventions, there is no unified protocol, and many patients discontinue therapy due to adverse events. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate preventive and reactive interventions for cutaneous adverse events in adult cancer patients receiving kinase inhibitors. A search was performed in MEDLINE (via PubMed), EMBASE, and CENTRAL (The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), using predefined search terms. Outcomes were incidence, severity of cutaneous adverse events (grades 1-4 and 3-4), quality of life and adherence to oncologic therapy. After screening 35,072 records, 9 studies (1853 patients, per protocol) met the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis, while 52 were included in the systematic review. Preventive topical agents significantly reduced the incidence of grade 1-4 cutaneous adverse events (OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.38-0.80; p = 0.012; I2 = 16%), whereas systemic interventions showed no significant benefit in this category. Conversely, for grade 3-4 events, systemic interventions were associated with a significantly reduced incidence (OR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.14-0.41; p = 0.002, I2 = 0%), while topical agents had no significant effect. For reactive interventions, no consistent evidence of effectiveness was found, with high heterogeneity and a limited number of studies. In patients receiving kinase inhibitors, systemic antibiotics were associated with a reduction in grade 3-4 cutaneous adverse events, while pooled topical interventions significantly reduced grade 1-4 events. However, the effectiveness of individual topical agents, including urea, remains uncertain.

papers.abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) is associated with morbidity, mortality, and interruptions to cancer treatment. Current cardio-oncology clinical assessment tools generally rely on a limited range of clinical data; however, in the era of precision medicine, it may be possible to leverage multimodal data, including imaging and multi-omic inputs, to personalise CTR-CVT prediction and assessment. In this review, we examine the genotypic and phenotypic predictors of CTR-CVT and the evidence supporting their incorporation into multimodal risk models. Most research focuses on cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). We identify a strong evidence base for multimodal imaging-guided prediction, particularly cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived global longitudinal strain measurements. Emerging evidence also supports the potential value of novel imaging parameters, including computed tomography (CT) and TTE-derived radiomic features. From the genomic and proteomic perspective, truncating titin variants and microRNA-126 may be informative predictors of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). At the same time, the literature also highlights potential epigenomic markers of CTR-CVT. Finally, we consider how these diverse data can be integrated into multimodal risk models and how digital innovation and advanced machine learning methods may further improve model predictive performance. However, a large implementation gap remains, with challenges such as data privacy and a lack of external validation studies preventing routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives:Pneumocystis jirovecii colonization induces persistent low-grade pulmonary inflammation, which may alter fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake in positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT). We aimed to evaluate whether asymptomatic infection influences the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) or clinicopathological parameters of primary lung cancer. Methods: In this prospective single-center observational study, 107 consecutive patients undergoing surgical resection for primary lung cancer were enrolled. Preoperative FDG PET/CT scans were obtained within four weeks prior to surgery. Intraoperative respiratory secretions and lung tissue samples were analyzed for P. jirovecii, using nested polymerase chain reaction (nested-PCR) targeting the mitochondrial large subunit rRNA gene. Propensity score matching (PSM) adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index was performed across 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 matching models. Results:Pneumocystis jirovecii colonization was confirmed in 12 of 107 patients (11.21%). In the unadjusted cohort, no significant differences in primary lesion SUVmax were identified between positive and negative patients (10.38 ± 6.50 vs. 8.86 ± 6.58, p = 0.411), nor across matched models (1:1: p = 0.555; 1:2: p = 0.951; 1:3: p = 0.926). Following PSM, patients without colonization exhibited significantly larger maximum tumor diameters in both 1:2 (30.71 ± 19.23 vs. 18.25 ± 6.63 mm, p = 0.035) and 1:3 matching models (29.08 ± 17.47 vs. 18.25 ± 6.63 mm, p = 0.035). Conclusions: We did not find any association between P. jirovecii colonization and preoperative metabolic tumor staging on FDG PET/CT. However, asymptomatic carriage was associated with smaller primary tumor dimensions following propensity adjustment in 1:2 and 1:3 matching models, warranting further exploration of host-fungal interactions within the pulmonary tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract: Dermoscopy improves the diagnosis of melanoma and keratinocyte carcinoma, but its value depends on the observer, the lesion mix, the anatomic site, and the action taken after the examination. Recent reviews have mainly focused on one modality or image-classification accuracy. This narrative review follows the clinical pathway and compares five linked areas: defined diagnostic criteria, sequential digital monitoring, site- and skin-tone-specific interpretation, multimodal imaging, and artificial intelligence (AI). Melanoma and keratinocyte carcinoma are discussed separately because their criteria, diagnostic problems, imaging needs, and management differ. Meta-analyses support dermoscopy over naked-eye examination, although accuracy remains closely related to clinician experience. A randomized trial of three-dimensional total-body photography with sequential dermoscopy led to more procedures and higher costs without finding more malignant tumors over two years. Reflectance confocal microscopy can improve specificity in selected equivocal lesions, while optical coherence technologies add architectural and depth information that is most relevant to keratinocyte carcinoma. AI has moved from retrospective benchmarks to prospective multicenter studies, but false-positive burden, dataset shift, underrepresentation of darker skin tones, limited explainability, and uncertain workflow effects remain. The review also considers foundation models, regulation, and patient-facing tools and uses a SWOT analysis to define research priorities. The field is at an inflection point in evidence, not image quality. Progress should be judged by effects on biopsy decisions, missed-cancer rates, timeliness, cost, access, and patient outcomes in defined populations.

papers.abstract: This review investigated whether exposure to certain endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) increases skin cancer risk. We performed a comprehensive narrative review of in vitro, animal, and human studies examining the association of EDCs with melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC). Chemicals are classified as (i) established EDCs with evidence of skin carcinogenicity; (ii) chemicals that are carcinogenic with endocrine-related effects; and (iii) chemicals with limited or uncertain evidence. Proposed carcinogenic mechanisms include oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, DNA repair inhibition, and epigenetic alterations; AhR likely mediates the carcinogenicity of dioxin (TCDD), dioxin-like PCBs, and PAHs. Epidemiological evidence linking PCBs with melanoma is inconsistent. High cumulative occupational exposure to PAH-containing mineral oils or tar/pitch increases skin cancer risk. Evidence for PFAS and skin cancer is limited and inconsistent. Increased melanoma incidence has been reported after chronic occupational exposure to certain pesticides, including carbaryl, parathion, and maneb/mancozeb. There is substantial evidence of a dose-response association between chronic arsenic exposure and NMSC risk. High chronic exposure to specific EDCs (especially arsenic, certain PAHs, and certain pesticides) may increase skin cancer risk. For several chemicals, evidence supports carcinogenicity with endocrine-related effects, but direct mechanistic evidence that endocrine disruption specifically mediates skin carcinogenesis is lacking.

papers.abstract: Background: Accumulating evidence suggests that vitamin D may influence cancer prognosis. We aimed to explore whether the TP53 codon 72 polymorphism (p.Pro72Arg; rs1042522) may be associated with differential effects of vitamin D supplementation on digestive tract cancer prognosis. Methods: This post hoc analysis of the AMATERASU randomized controlled trial included patients in whom both germline TP53 codon 72 genotype and p53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assessment were available. Patients were stratified according to TP53 codon 72 genotype and p53 IHC expression. The association between vitamin D supplementation and relapse-free survival (RFS) was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression models within each subgroup. Results: A total of 333 participants (79.9%) out of 417 in the AMATERASU trial were included in the analysis. RFS was comparable between the vitamin D and placebo groups across the TP53 codon 72 genotype subgroups. The vitamin D group was significantly associated with more favorable RFS compared with the placebo group in patients with both the Arg/Arg genotype and high p53 IHC expression (HR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87; p = 0.03). However, with a fragility index of 2 and a non-significant three-way interaction among vitamin D supplementation, p53 IHC expression, and the Arg/Arg genotype (p for interaction = 0.09), these findings remain fragile despite reaching statistical significance, warranting careful interpretation. Conclusions: Vitamin D supplementation was associated with more favorable RFS among patients with digestive tract cancer who had both the Arg/Arg genotype and high p53 IHC expression. These exploratory findings warrant further investigation in prospective studies.

papers.abstract: Background: Breast cancer progression is strongly influenced by tumor cell interactions with the extracellular matrix (ECM). Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture models provide more relevant systems for studying aspects of the tumor microenvironment (TME), including tumor architecture, matrix remodeling and cell-ECM communication. Collagen type I (Col I), fibronectin (FN) and hyaluronan (HA) are key ECM components involved in breast cancer progression. At the same time, integrins act as major matrix-sensing receptors that translate ECM cues into cellular responses. In this study, we investigated how defined ECM contexts regulate functional cell properties in shERβ MDA-MB-231 and Hs578T advanced 3D breast cancer cell models. Methods: Cells were cultured in 2D and 3D systems under matrix-free conditions or in Col I, FN, and mixed Col I/FN environments, in the presence or absence of HA or sulfated HA (sHA). Spheroid growth, matrix-dependent spheroid organization and dissemination were evaluated. In parallel, selected collagen- and fibronectin-associated integrin subunits, together with HA-related molecules including HAS2, CD44, and RHAMM, were analyzed to assess receptor-mediated matrix- and HA-associated responses. Results: Matrix substrates strongly influenced breast cancer spheroid behavior. Col I promoted outward dissemination, whereas FN-containing environments favored compact organization and restricted spreading. HA supported spheroid-like organization in a matrix-dependent manner, whereas sHA disrupted organized spheroid assembly in ECM-rich conditions, resulting in looser structures or smaller cell colonies, depending on the matrix context. Gene expression analysis revealed model-dependent remodeling of matrix- and HA-associated programs, with broader adhesion-related responses in shERβ MDA-MB-231 cells and stronger dimensionality-driven regulation in Hs578T cells. Conclusions: Overall, these findings demonstrate that defined ECM contexts actively regulate breast cancer spheroid behavior and matrix-associated receptor programs. Col I, FN and mixed Col I/FN environments generated distinct 3D phenotypes, affecting spheroid growth, organization and dissemination, while HA/sHA further modified these matrix-dependent responses. This study supports sHA as a functional matrix molecule with anti-cancer relevance and highlights the value of 3D matrix-based models for investigating tumor-matrix communication in breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, largely due to high recurrence rates and the development of therapy-resistant disease. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) contribute to treatment failure by promoting chemoresistance through signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, Hedgehog, and Notch, as well as through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment (TME). Ovarian CSC (OCSC)-associated biomarkers, including CD44, CD24, CD133, and ALDH, have expanded opportunities for specific tumor characterization and biomarker identification. Effective targeting of OCSCs requires experimental models that preserve cellular plasticity and hierarchical organization. Development of synthetic matrices and chemically defined media has improved the reproducibility and scalability of three-dimensional (3D) organoid cultures for preclinical drug testing. CSC-derived organoids, established by enriching cells positive for CSC markers directly from patient tumor material, provide a 3D platform for studying OCSC-associated phenotypes and therapeutic responses. This review examines current understanding of ovarian CSC biology and the development of OCSC-derived 3D organoid models that can recapitulate cellular architecture and patient-specific drug responses. These 3D organoid models provide a guided platform for evaluating emerging therapeutics, such as micropeptides encoded by short open reading frames or engineered from functional tumor-suppressor protein domains selected to target OCSCs. Their small size enables modulation of intracellular signaling and highly specific protein-protein interactions. We further review micropeptide stabilization strategies and tumor-targeted delivery systems designed to enhance bioavailability. This review highlights how integrating patient-specific OCSC-derived organoid models with engineered micropeptides may accelerate the development of personalized treatment strategies for ovarian cancer while improving the preclinical evaluation of novel therapies.

papers.abstract: Background: Accurate axillary response prediction is clinically relevant in clinically node-positive (cN+) breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant chemo-(immuno)therapy (NAC). This study evaluated the value of [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic characteristics and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) to predict axillary pathologic complete response (pCR). Second, the association between [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic characteristics and TILs was evaluated. Methods: This retrospective study included cN+ breast cancer patients treated with NAC and axillary surgery from the prospective multicentre RISAS trial (NCT02800317). Baseline [18F]FDG PET/CT-derived metabolic activity of the breast tumour, axillary lymph node metastases (ALNMs), and spleen was assessed, together with TILs measured in the breast tumour and ALNMs. TILs were classified as low (<10%) versus high (≥10%). Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results: Of 135 patients, 46 (34.1%) achieved axillary pCR. Higher liver mean tumour-to-background ratio (2.7 vs. 1.9, p = 0.042), trends towards higher breast and ALNM maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax), lower splenic SUVmax and high breast tumour TILs were associated with axillary pCR. Multivariable logistic regression combining tumour grade, subtype, maximum spleen-to-liver ratio, and breast tumour TILs yielded an apparent area under the curve of 0.80 [95%CI 0.73-0.88]. Higher ALNM SUVmax and SUVmean (10.5 vs. 6.3, p = 0.024; 6.4 vs. 3.7, p = 0.015) and lower splenic SUVmean (2.6 vs. 3.1, p = 0.035) were associated with high breast tumour TILs. Conclusions: A model combining clinicopathological, metabolic, and immune-related characteristics may be informative for predicting axillary response to NAC but did not perform better than clinicopathological characteristics alone. Future studies should evaluate whether accurate prediction models can support safe axillary treatment de-escalation.

papers.abstract: Upfront allogeneic stem cell transplantation (allo-SCT) without pretransplant cytoreduction is an established concept in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes with increased blasts (MDS-IB), but the optimal conditioning strategy remains to be defined. While fludarabine and treosulfan (Flu/Treo) has become an established regimen for older patients based on its favorable ratio between toxicity and efficacy, its impact when used in the context of upfront transplant is less well described. Here, we retrospectively investigated Flu/Treo as the backbone for conditioning in 35 patients with MDS-IB (median blast count 13%) receiving upfront transplantation. Outcomes in this high-risk cohort (75% IPSS-M high or very high) were promising, with an estimated 2-year overall (OS), relapse-free survival (RFS) and non-relapse mortality (NRM) of 76%, 56% and 13%, respectively. Relapse was the major cause of treatment failure, reflected by a relapse incidence (CIR) of 31%. We identified the TP53 mutation status as the main driver of relapse (2-year RFS TP53 mutated 17% vs. 67%, p = 0.01; 2-year CIR 54% vs. 24%, p = 0.08) and an adverse prognostic factor, while the pretransplant blast count did not affect the post-transplant outcome. Intensification with the addition of melphalan (Mel, n = 18) to a sequential conditioning approach did not improve the outcome (Mel vs. Flu/Treo 2-year OS 62% vs. 87%, RFS 50% vs. 63%, CIR 37% vs. 24%, NRM 14% vs. 12%, all not significant). This pilot series shows that upfront transplantation using Flu/Treo conditioning in high-risk MDS patients facilitates promising post-transplant outcomes and may serve as a backbone to further improve these results through innovative peri-transplant interventions.

papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among cancer survivors. Contemporary cardio-oncology frameworks emphasize baseline cardiovascular risk assessment before potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapies. Historical real world implementation of baseline electrocardiography (ECG), however, remains incompletely characterized. The objective of this study was to characterize historical baseline ECG ascertainment before cancer diagnosis and examine its association with documented cardiovascular diagnosis patterns in cancer survivors. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 4592 adult cancer survivors within the Froedtert & Medical College of Wisconsin health system from 2000 to 2020. The analytic cohort was derived from a previously established longitudinal cancer survivor resource integrating demographic and cardiovascular clinical data, cancer treatment exposures, multimodality cardiac function ascertainment, and linked clinical, radiation oncology, and cancer registry information. Cardiac function ascertainment from an available cardiovascular imaging modality within three years before cancer diagnosis was one component of the analytic cohort definition. Patients were stratified by ascertainment of a 12-lead ECG within the same pre-diagnostic interval. Cardiovascular diagnoses documented before and after cancer diagnosis were characterized separately. For the newly documented diagnosis analyses, each cardiovascular outcome was evaluated among participants without a prior diagnosis of that same condition before cancer diagnosis. A multivariable logistic regression model evaluated the association between baseline ECG ascertainment and newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (including HF, AFIB, CAD, and stroke) while adjusting for age, sex, race, comorbidity count, and treatment count. Among 4592 individuals, 3726 (81%) had a baseline ECG. ECG ascertainment was associated with older age and greater pre-existing cardiovascular and cardiometabolic burden. The available follow up distributions were similar between patients without and with baseline ECG ascertainment (748 [Q1 258, Q3 1781] vs. 767 [Q1 219, Q3 1822] days; p > 0.9). In multivariable analysis, baseline ECG ascertainment was associated with lower odds of a newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.31-0.46); this odds ratio represents an association rather than a time-specific risk or protective effect. Baseline ECGs were commonly ascertainable within this longitudinal cancer survivor cohort and identified groups with different pre-existing cardiovascular burden and subsequent cardiovascular diagnosis patterns. These findings provide a historical benchmark for cardiovascular assessment in cancer care and support prospective patient-level studies integrating ECG findings with clinical and oncologic risk factors to refine cardiovascular surveillance strategies across cancer survivorship.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of cancer. The predictive performance of baseline D-dimer and factors influencing its levels among patients with cancer remain unclear. We aimed to identify predictors of subsequent VTE development and evaluate the cancer-specific predictive performance of baseline D-dimer. Methods: This retrospective study included 23,505 patients with any of 11 malignancies who underwent baseline D-dimer measurement at initial diagnosis at Gifu University Hospital between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients with pre-existing VTE were excluded. Predictors were identified using logistic regression analyses. Cancer-specific predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analyses, with optimal cutoff values determined by the Youden index. Factors associated with baseline D-dimer were also assessed. Results: The median follow-up was 45.3 months (30.4-59.1 months), during which VTE occurred in 784 (3.3%) patients. Higher baseline D-dimer levels and distant metastasis were independent predictors of subsequent VTE. Cancer type was significantly associated with VTE overall, and breast cancer was associated with lower odds than esophageal cancer. D-dimer performance varied among cancer types, with optimal cutoff values of 0.55-2.35 μg/mL. Older age and higher platelet counts were independently associated with elevated baseline D-dimer levels, whereas a higher cholesterol level was inversely associated. Conclusions: Baseline D-dimer level is an independent predictor of subsequent VTE in patients with cancer. Its predictive performance and exploratory thresholds vary among cancers, suggesting that cancer type should be considered when interpreting baseline D-dimer levels. External validation is required before these cancer-specific thresholds can be applied clinically.

papers.abstract: The incidence of p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is increasing, with improved prognosis compared to non-HPV-related cancers. Standard treatment of locally advanced OPSCC involves high-dose cisplatin (HDC) with radiation but is associated with significant toxicity. Low-dose cisplatin (LDC) administered weekly has shown comparable efficacy to HDC in prior studies. This study evaluates the real-world outcomes of LDC in p16-positive OPSCC in a regional centre. Patients treated with curative radiation and concurrent LDC (40 mg/m2 weekly) for p16-positive OPSCC from January 2015 to December 2021 were retrospectively analysed (n = 103). Primary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), with secondary endpoints being loco-regional and distant recurrence rates, and chemotherapy-related toxicity. Overall survival rates were 94%, 89%, and 84% at two, three, and five years, respectively. The progression-free survival rates were 90%, 83%, and 80% over the same periods. The low-risk group showed excellent outcomes with no loco-regional recurrences and low distant relapse rates (6% at 5 years). The intermediate-risk group had higher loco-regional recurrences (10% at 5 years) and a similar distant relapse rate (7% at 5 years). T4 or N3 disease patients had lower survival and higher distant relapse rates but excellent loco-regional control. The median cumulative cisplatin dose was 240 mg/m2, with no survival difference between those receiving ≥200 mg/m2 versus less. Toxicity led to dose reductions (8%), delays (13%), and early cessations (30%). LDC is effective for p16-positive OPSCC with manageable toxicity, showing outcomes comparable to outcomes previously reported in studies using HDC.
