papers.abstract: Breast cancer exhibits marked molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity, with important implications for prognosis and therapeutic response. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used for detection and staging, its potential role as a prognostic biomarker across molecular subtypes remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the association between MRI-defined tumor imaging phenotypes and disease-free survival (DFS) among different breast cancer molecular subtypes. This retrospective single-center study included 407 patients with invasive breast carcinoma of no special type who underwent pre-treatment breast MRI between October 2015 and May 2021. Tumors were classified into molecular subtypes and three MRI phenotypes based on lesion morphology and distribution. Associations between imaging phenotype, molecular subtype, and DFS were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Type 3 was the most prevalent imaging phenotype overall (60%), followed by Type 2 (21.9%) and Type 1 (18.2%). Imaging phenotype distribution differed significantly among molecular subtypes. Over a median follow-up of 57 months, imaging phenotype was not associated with DFS in Luminal A, Luminal B, or HER2-overexpressed tumors. However, in the triple-negative/ER-low subgroup, imaging phenotype demonstrated an independent association with DFS. In multivariable analysis, patients with the Type 1 phenotype had an 8.16-fold higher risk of recurrence compared with those with the Type 2 phenotype (95% CI: 1.49-44.60; p = 0.015). Type 2 lesions showed the most favorable survival outcomes. In this exploratory analysis, MRI phenotype was associated with disease-free survival in triple-negative and ER-low breast cancers. Circumscribed, unifocal tumors are associated with improved survival, whereas spiculated or multifocal patterns are associated with worse outcomes. However, given the small number of events in this subgroup, these exploratory findings need to be confirmed in larger studies before MRI morphology can be considered a prognostic imaging biomarker in aggressive breast cancer subtypes.

papers.abstract: The clinical utility of genomic profiling in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) remains incompletely defined, particularly for clinically relevant annotated alterations and prognostic stratification. We performed a multi-institutional analysis to characterize genomic alterations across GEP-NEN subtypes, generate prevalence estimates to inform precision oncology efforts, and evaluate associations with clinical actionability and survival. We performed a retrospective analysis of 1,691 GEP-NENs from the American Association for Cancer Research Project Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange database. Tumors were classified into neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) or neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs) and stratified by primary site. Genomic alterations, including single-nucleotide variants, insertions/deletions, copy number alterations, and structural variants, were analyzed using a panel-adjusted approach. Alterations were annotated for clinical relevance using multiple knowledge bases. Overall survival was evaluated in a subset (n = 502) with available data. Genomic alterations were identified in 86.5% of patients. NETs were enriched for alterations in chromatin-remodeling genes (MEN1, DAXX) and mTOR pathway regulator TSC2, whereas NECs were characterized by canonical drivers (TP53, RB1, KRAS, APC, and BRAF). Annotated alterations were identified in 34.1% of all patients, with higher rates in NECs compared with NETs (74.4% v 28.5%, P < .001). Notable annotated targets included BRAF V600E (2.2%; 14.8% of all colorectal NECs), KRAS-activating mutations (6.8%; 0.35% G12C), and NTRK fusions (0.2%). Annotation rates varied by primary site with the highest rates observed in colorectal, gastric, and esophageal NECs. In NETs, the presence of NEC-associated driver alterations was associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio, 3.67 [95% CI, 2.49 to 5.42], P < .001). Genomic profiling reveals meaningful differences in biomarker prevalence and prognosis across GEP-NEN subtypes. These findings support integrating genomic profiling with histologic classification to refine risk stratification and inform biomarker-driven clinical trials.

papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection has been implicated in vocal fold leukoplakia (VFL), a precancerous laryngeal lesion. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between H. pylori and VFL, focusing on the NRF2/KEAP1 oxidative stress pathway. Clinicopathological analysis was performed on samples from 64 patients with VFL and 30 patients with vocal cord polyps (controls). The results showed a significantly higher prevalence of H. pylori in the VFL group (48.4%) than in the controls (16.7%, p = 0.003). Among H. pylori-positive VFL cases, VacA-positive strains predominated, accounting for 71.0%. Multivariate logistic regression identified H. pylori as an independent risk factor for VFL (OR = 6.198, 95% CI: 1.580-24.321). VFL tissues exhibited upregulated expression of NRF2, KEAP1, and HO-1 (p < 0.001), demonstrating both virulence-dependent (HO-1 induction) and virulence-independent (NRF2 upregulation) pathway activation patterns. In vitro experiments revealed that H. pylori exposure induced NRF2 nuclear translocation and triggered an oxidative stress response. Notably, VFL-derived cells responded more rapidly to H. pylori stimulation, with pathway activation peaking at 24 h post-infection, whereas normal cells showed a delayed response, peaking at 48 h (p < 0.05). Furthermore, VFL-derived cells displayed more pronounced stress-induced morphological alterations following H. pylori exposure. These findings suggest that H. pylori may promote VFL progression via NRF2/KEAP1 pathway activation, highlighting the potential clinical value of H. pylori screening in VFL management.

papers.abstract: Barrett's esophagus (BE) patients require improved cancer risk stratification to identify high-risk individuals while reducing over-treatment in low-risk populations. BE evolution towards adenocarcinoma is likely driven by a combination of genomic and microenvironmental factors, suggesting the potential of predictive models that integrate both. Here, we developed BEACON (Barrett's Esophagus DNA content Abnormality and immune ecology for Cancer Outcome), a spatially aware framework integrating deep learning-based prediction of DNA content and immune architecture from routine histopathology. First, DACOR, a multi-instance learning model that predicts DNA content from histopathology, was trained using 777 BE biopsies with flow cytometry-based DNA content data scanned at two institutions, and it demonstrated strong performance across both validation and test datasets for DNA content abnormality prediction. Patients classified as DNA content abnormal by DACOR demonstrated increased cancer progression. Complementary models for cell classification and tissue segmentation enabled spatial immune ecology metric computations. Abnormal regions exhibited increased lymphoplasmacytic inflammation versus normal regions. Among patients with DNA content abnormality, cancer progressors exhibited increased plasma cell clustering adjacent to abnormal epithelium compared to non-progressors. Finally, a logistic regression model was developed that integrated molecular, immune ecological, and epithelial morphology features for cancer risk stratification. The integrated risk classification model stratified DNA content abnormal patients into high- and low-risk groups that corresponded with progression and patient survival. Overall, BEACON spatially integrates molecular abnormality with immune ecology to stratify BE patients by cancer progression risk using routine pathology images.

papers.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy is a promising cancer treatment that elicits antitumor immunity. However, the efficacy of virotherapy is often constrained by tumor-intrinsic immune suppression. To identify conserved virus-induced programs driving immune escape, we applied multi-omics and functional assays across multiple tumor and virus models, uncovering an SLC3A2-driven immunosuppressive metabolic barrier. In oncolytic herpes simplex virus (oHSV)-infected tumors, a biphasic immune trajectory emerged: early CD8+ T cell activation was followed by SLC3A2-mediated methionine and tryptophan uptake, driving T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, oHSV upregulated SLC3A2 via the m6A-IGF2BP3 axis, while tumor-intrinsic tryptophan metabolism engaged the AHR/ARNT/ICP4 cascade to amplify viral replication and reinforce the immunosuppressive program. Importantly, dietary methionine supplementation disrupted the metabolic checkpoint, restored T cell effector function, and synergized with oHSV expressing anti-PD1 to enhance tumor control in humanized preclinical models. Notably, a parallel SLC3A2-centered metabolic-immunologic circuit operated in vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) infection. Together, these findings delineate an actionable, conserved metabolic checkpoint and provide a framework for integrating metabolic modulation into cancer viroimmunotherapy.

After a median follow-up of 14.3 months, the median progression-free survival was 9.8 months and 5.7 months, respectively.

papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is a well-described hallmark of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Gene copy number variation and altered gene expression data suggest enhanced branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) transamination and reduced BCAA oxidation are highly selected traits in ccRCC. Surprisingly, we found that genetic modulation of BCAA oxidation had little effect on experimental ccRCC cell growth in vitro and in vivo. In contrast, BCAA transamination in ccRCC cells was essential for the generation of glutamate-derived glutathione and cell viability when glutamine was limiting. Thus, BCAA transamination conferred resistance to states of low glutamine or treatment with the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 by providing glutathione independent of glutamine breakdown. Targeting BCAA transamination in vitro and in vivo sensitized ccRCC to CB-839 mediated glutaminase inhibition by decreasing glutathione biosynthesis and redox homeostasis. These findings reveal that BCAA transamination maintains critical glutamate and glutathione levels in glutamine-deprived ccRCC, explaining why CB-839 treatment has been ineffective in ccRCC clinical trials and demonstrate an approach to treat ccRCC by targeting BCAA transamination to create a vulnerability to glutaminase inhibition.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Despite their benefit, current anti-EGFR therapies are limited by narrow efficacy profiles due to dose-limiting toxicities. This phase 2 open-label study evaluated the efficacy and safety of ABT-806, an EGFR-targeting antibody that is tumor specific, in patients with advanced EGFR-expressing tumors including head and neck cancers (H&NC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of other sites. Methods: Patients with advanced H&NC (cohort A) or SCC of other sites (cohort B) were enrolled in the study. ABT-806 was administered as monotherapy at a dose of 24 mg/kg intravenously using a twice weekly dosing schedule until unacceptable toxicity and/or evidence of disease progression. Adverse events (AEs) were graded using the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v4.0; tumor response was assessed using the Response Evaluation criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1. EGFR status was assessed with mAb806 and EGFRvIII immunohistochemistry and correlated with outcomes. Results: ABT-806 was well tolerated with no grade 3+ treatment-related AEs. Disease stabilization was observed in two patients (14%) and for a median duration of 19.5 weeks. This included one patient from cohort A and one patient from cohort B. Progression-free survival and overall survival was not significantly different between the two cohorts. Conclusions: Although clinical activity was limited in this small, heavily pre-treated, and biomarker-unselected population, ABT-806 demonstrated an excellent safety profile with minimal classical EGFR-related toxicity. These findings support the development of more tumor-specific EGFR antibodies for use, particularly in combinatorial regimens.

papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical characteristics and prognostic significance of distinct Ki-67 proliferation indices in patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). Methods: A retrospective analysis of clinical data from 307 NDMM patients admitted to the Second Hospital of Shanxi Medical University from January 2015 to December 2023. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on Ki-67 proliferation index: Ki-67 > 10% and Ki-67 ≤ 10%. Results: Among the 307 enrolled NDMM patients, 199 (64.82%, 199/307) were assigned to the Ki-67 ≤ 10% group. The median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 45.52 months (95% CI: 39.40-51.66) in the Ki-67 ≤ 10% group, compared with 25.81 months (95% CI: 20.61-31.00) in the Ki-67 > 10% group, with a statistically significant difference in PFS between the two cohorts (p 10% group, with a statistically significant difference in OS between the two cohorts (p 10% have a significantly worse prognosis than those with Ki-67 ≤ 10%. A high Ki-67 index (>10%) is identified as an independent adverse prognostic parameter for NDMM. Furthermore, the integration of Ki-67 proliferation index with ISS staging can substantially enhance the accuracy of prognostic risk stratification in patients with NDMM.

papers.abstract: Lipid mediators are small molecules, derived from lipid metabolism, that initiate cellular responses. In this review, the major classes of lipid mediators are considered with respect to their effects on prostate cancer cells. These classes are: sphingolipids (sphingosine 1-phosphate and ceramide), glycophospholipids (lysophosphatidic acid; LPA), eicosanoids (prostaglandins, thromboxanes, and leukotrienes), cannabinoids, and free fatty acids. Almost all of these mediators elicit effects by binding to druggable G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to initiate cell proliferation, stimulate migration, and enhance survival. The exceptions are omega-3 fatty acids and endocannabinoids, which inhibit proliferation. The mediators and their receptors serve as potential targets for (1) enzyme inhibitors that block their synthesis, or (2) GPCR antagonists or agonists. These agents are in various stages of development. Progress in testing their translational potential varies between the mediator classes. Lipid mediators also show potential as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers. Interesting mechanistic aspects have been identified in the course of studying lipid mediator responses in prostate cancer cells. These include positive cross-talk between LPA receptors and EGF receptors, and negative cross-talk between LPA receptors and free fatty acid (FFA) receptors. Together, these findings suggest new strategies for modulating prostate cancer growth and survival pathways in a therapeutic direction.

papers.abstract: Multiportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was introduced in Japan in the 1990s, with uniportal VATS (U-VATS) and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) following in the 2010s. U-VATS gained significant traction after the 1st Fellowship of the Japanese Association for Chest Surgery (JACS; currently the Japanese Society for Thoracic Surgery, JSTS) in 2018, leading to the establishment of the Japanese Uniportal VATS Interest Group (JUVIG) in April 2018. JUVIG has since driven wider adoption through extensive activities, including educational programs, publications, and collaborative multicenter studies. As a result, expert surgeons now utilize U-VATS for complex procedures such as bronchoplasty, completion lobectomy, complex segmentectomy, and pediatric surgery. Concurrently, RATS gained insurance coverage in Japan in 2018 and has become more prevalent than U-VATS. Despite the significant costs associated with RATS, its adoption rate surpasses that of U-VATS due to institutional policies, perceived ease of implementation, branding, recruitment incentives, and recent national healthcare insurance reimbursement revisions (add-ons) introduced in 2026, which may create administrative pressure to prioritize robotic cases. Although reduced-port RATS is gaining popularity-blurring the lines with U-VATS-and newly emerging indigenous robotic platforms are expected to further accelerate RATS adoption, multiportal VATS (M-VATS) remains the dominant approach in many institutions. Furthermore, maintaining proficiency in VATS, U-VATS, and open thoracotomy remains indispensable for surgical education, economic viability, and acute intraoperative crisis management. Ultimately, while U-VATS represents a promising minimally invasive option, its widespread adoption for major and complex resections in Japan continues to be restricted by both educational and societal barriers.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th edition subdivides node-positive periampullary adenocarcinoma into N1 and N2 by the number of positive nodes. We quantified how much this subdivision and the lymph node ratio (LNR) each add to nodal positivity, and how the nodal yield affects the comparison. Methods: This retrospective cohort comprised 147 consecutive pancreatoduodenectomies for pancreatic head (n = 49), distal bile duct (n = 63), ampullary (n = 31) or duodenal (n = 4) adenocarcinoma. In covariate-adjusted Cox models stratified by origin, the N1/N2 subdivision and the LNR were tested over nodal positivity and over each other with nested likelihood-ratio tests, overall, with the examined-node count in the model and by the period of resection. Results: The median nodal yield was 17 (10 in 2013-2016, 19 in 2017-2024). Beyond nodal positivity, the N1/N2 subdivision added χ2 0.25 (p = 0.61; adjusted N2-versus-N1 hazard ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-2.45) and the LNR added χ2 9.60 (p = 0.002; hazard ratio 1.41 per 0.1, 95% CI 1.22-1.62). The LNR added to the N category (p = 0.002; optimism-corrected C-index gain 0.020, 95% CI 0.002-0.041), whereas the N category did not add detectably to the LNR (p = 0.54). With the examined-node count in the model, the LNR increment was attenuated (p = 0.045) and the subdivision's increment rose (χ2 3.65, p = 0.056). From 2017 onward (n = 113), the LNR and the positive-node count were nearly collinear among the node-positive patients (ρ 0.90 versus -0.02 before 2017), and neither the subdivision (p = 0.49) nor the LNR (p = 0.17) added significantly to positivity. Conclusions: The N1/N2 subdivision added little beyond nodal positivity, although imprecisely estimated, and its increment rose when the examined-node count was in the model. The LNR added prognostic information mainly when the yield was low or variable; where the yield was higher and more uniform, the ratio and the count-based category conveyed nearly the same information, and no additional value of the ratio was demonstrated.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The HER2-low classification has redefined therapeutic strategies, but its prognostic significance remains uncertain. We compared overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) across HER2 categories (HER2-low, HER2-negative, HER2-positive) in a real-world cohort. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study conducted at a high-complexity cancer center in Colombia; it included 373 patients with invasive breast cancer classified as HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+), HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-), or HER2-negative (IHC 0). Survival was estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Multivariable Cox models were adjusted for age, clinical stage, histological grade, and hormone receptor status, and PFS was additionally analyzed separately in stage I-III and stage IV disease. Results: The cohort included HER2-low (38.3%), HER2-negative (39.7%), and HER2-positive (22.0%) tumors. HER2-low tumors showed lower grade and higher hormone receptor expression (p < 0.001), without better survival. Three-year OS (81.8%, 76.5%, 62.8%; p = 0.178) and PFS (p = 0.227) did not differ. Advanced stage remained the main determinant of mortality, whereas the association with high grade was attenuated. HER2-low was not independently associated with OS (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.31-1.45) or PFS (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.40-1.49). Hormone receptor positivity was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.43; 95% CI 0.21-0.88). PFS did not differ across HER2 categories in stage I-III (p = 0.307) or stage IV disease (p = 0.068). Conclusions: HER2-low status was not independently associated with survival. Its more favorable clinicopathological profile was largely explained by higher hormone receptor expression, which was itself associated with survival once included in the models.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This is the first study in Eastern Europe to integrate skin and iris phenotypic characteristics with selected polymorphisms in genes related to skin aging, melanogenesis and skin pigmentation, and inflammatory regulation in relation to cutaneous melanoma (CM) risk. Methods: This case-control study included 180 patients with primary CM identified from the Hospital of the LSMU Kauno klinikos database and 181 controls without a personal history of skin cancer selected from a population-based study in Kaunas. All participants underwent dermatological and ophthalmological examinations and completed questionnaires assessing sun-exposure habits, including severe sunburn history, and Fitzpatrick skin phototype. The total-body number of common melanocytic nevi (CMN) >2 mm in diameter and the number of iris freckles were evaluated using standardized protocols. Five selected genetic polymorphisms, including TYR rs1126809, SLC45A2 rs26722, SLC45A2 rs16891982, IL6 rs1800795, and TNF-α rs1800629, were genotyped. Associations with CM were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results: We identified three phenotypical factors independently associated with increased odds of CM (OR; 95% CI): a total-body CMN count >15 (7.89; 4.29-14.53), ≥4 iris freckles (3.70; 2.04-6.74), and a history of severe sunburn (2.76; 1.50-5.07). Compared with Fitzpatrick skin phototype IV, phototypes II (0.35; 0.15-0.82) and III (0.28; 0.11-0.70) were associated with decreased CM odds. In the multivariable model the heterozygous SLC45A2 rs16891982 genotype was associated with increased CM odds (6.64; 1.48-29.83), while the IL6 rs1800795 Mono G genotype revealed an inverse association with CM (0.39; 0.16-0.97). Conclusions: A total-body CMN count >15, ≥4 iris freckles, and severe sunburn history revealed strong independent associations with increased CM risk. However, associations involving SLC45A2 rs16891982 and IL6 rs1800795 in this Lithuanian case-control study were model-dependent. These findings highlight the potential value of integrating selected genetic markers with phenotypic characteristics and sun-exposure history in the development of personalized CM risk prediction models; however, validation in larger populations is required.

papers.abstract: Observation is generally recommended for asymptomatic meningiomas, but evidence from incidental meningiomas is derived largely from heterogeneous intracranial locations and may not directly apply to tumors involving the anterior visual pathway. We investigated whether preoperative visual status remained associated with postoperative visual function after adjustment for baseline clinical and anatomical differences in this location-specific subgroup. We retrospectively reviewed 146 patients who underwent resection of skull base meningiomas contacting or compressing the optic nerve and/or chiasm. Preoperative visual status was categorized by comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluation as normal visual function or visual dysfunction. The primary outcome was postoperative normal visual function, defined as preservation of normal vision in patients with normal preoperative visual function and complete recovery in those with preoperative visual dysfunction. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, and propensity score matching was conducted using age, sex, tumor volume, tumor laterality, and optic canal involvement. Propensity score matching yielded 48 matched pairs with adequate balance across all measured covariates (all standardized mean differences < 0.1). Postoperative normal visual function was preserved or achieved in 95.8% of patients with normal preoperative visual function versus 31.3% of those with preoperative visual dysfunction (exact McNemar p < 0.001). Favorable visual outcome occurred in 95.8% versus 77.1%, respectively (p = 0.0225). Among surgically treated patients, normal preoperative visual function remained strongly associated with postoperative normal visual function after adjustment for measured clinical and anatomical differences. These findings do not establish that earlier surgery improves visual outcomes or define an optimal surgical timing strategy, but suggest that preoperative visual status and tumor anatomy should be considered in individualized management decisions.

papers.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge and a leading cause of mortality worldwide. As incidence continues to rise, early detection remains one of the most effective strategies for improving survival and reducing disease burden. Urine is an attractive source of biomarkers due to its non-invasive collection, ease of repeated sampling, and rich molecular composition. This scoping review evaluates the current landscape of urinary biomarkers for the early detection of cancer and their potential for clinical translation. A detailed literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science to identify studies investigating urinary biomarkers for cancer detection. Biomarkers were categorised by analyte class, and diagnostic performance, validation status, and clinical applicability were assessed. Urinary biomarkers demonstrated diagnostic potential across multiple malignancies, including lung, breast, pancreatic, hepatobiliary, colorectal, renal and ovarian cancers, while several urinary assays are already clinically available for bladder and prostate cancers. Promising diagnostic accuracy was reported for multiple biomarker classes, particularly multimarker panels integrating metabolites, proteins, nucleic acids, and epigenetic signatures. However, most studies were exploratory, involving small cohorts, methodological heterogeneity, and limited independent validation. Urinary biomarkers represent a promising and rapidly evolving approach to non-invasive cancer detection. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, few candidates have progressed to clinical implementation. Large prospective multicentre studies, rigorous validation, and assay standardisation are essential to establish urinary biomarkers as reliable tools for cancer screening, early diagnosis, and risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pathological response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is an established prognostic factor in locally advanced gastric cancer, but it does not fully reflect the biological heterogeneity of residual disease. The immune microenvironment may provide additional prognostic information. We therefore investigated the relationship between post-neoadjuvant Immunoscore, pathological findings, and disease-free survival in patients with microsatellite-stable locally advanced gastric cancer. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included patients with locally advanced gastric adenocarcinoma who received four cycles of neoadjuvant FLOT followed by curative-intent gastrectomy between November 2023 and May 2025. Immunoscore was determined in post-neoadjuvant resection specimens based on CD3+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the tumor center and invasive margin. Immunoscore assessments were performed by two pathologists blinded to clinical and outcome data, with final evaluations established through consensus review. Associations between Immunoscore and clinicopathological features were examined, including exploratory multivariable analyses adjusting for baseline clinical T stage and histological subtype. Disease-free survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results: The final analysis included 48 patients. Compared with the low-Immunoscore group, the high-Immunoscore group had lower rates of ypT4 disease (37.5% vs. 75.0%; p = 0.014), ypN3 disease (21.9% vs. 68.8%; p = 0.002), and perineural invasion (43.8% vs. 75.0%; p = 0.041). The association between low Immunoscore and ypN3 disease persisted after adjustment for baseline clinical T stage and histological subtype (adjusted OR 5.89, 95% CI 1.32-26.23; p = 0.020). Tumor regression grade did not differ significantly between the groups (p = 0.211). During a median follow-up of 18.0 months, 17 patients developed recurrence. Disease-free survival was numerically longer in the high-Immunoscore group. The difference was not significant by the log-rank test (p = 0.100), whereas an exploratory Breslow analysis showed a difference between the survival distributions (p = 0.025). However, Cox regression did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with disease-free survival (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.18-1.21; p = 0.117). Conclusions: A higher post-neoadjuvant Immunoscore was associated with less advanced residual tumor and nodal disease and less frequent perineural invasion, without a statistically significant association with tumor regression grade or disease-free survival in the primary analyses. Immunoscore may therefore complement conventional pathological assessment after neoadjuvant FLOT. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

papers.abstract: Background: Evidence regarding EUS-guided intratumoral phosphorus-32 (P-32) microparticle implantation for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC) remains limited. This prospective pilot study evaluated its technical feasibility, preliminary safety, and early disease-control outcomes when administered in combination with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel. Methods: Seventeen patients with unresectable LAPC underwent EUS-guided intratumoral P-32 microparticle implantation through a 22-gauge fine-needle aspiration needle during the fourth week of systemic chemotherapy. Intratumoral distribution was assessed using Bremsstrahlung SPECT/CT. Tumour response was evaluated according to RECIST version 1.1, and treatment-emergent adverse events were graded according to CTCAE version 4.0. The main secondary endpoint was local disease control rate at approximately 16 weeks (LDCR16w). All analyses were descriptive. Results: Implantation was technically successful in all 17 patients (100.0%; exact 95% CI, 80.5-100.0%), and SPECT/CT confirmed intratumoral distribution in every case. No implantation-related procedural complications were recorded (0/17; exact 95% CI, 0.0-19.5%). At approximately 16 weeks, CT assessment was available for 16 patients: seven had a partial response and nine had stable disease. The LDCR16w was 16/16 among evaluable patients (100.0%; exact 95% CI, 79.4-100.0%) and 16/17 in the all-treated analysis (94.1%; exact 95% CI, 71.3-99.9%). A reduction in CA19-9 of at least 50% was observed in 13/16 evaluable patients. Four patients underwent subsequent R0 resection (4/17, 23.5%; exact 95% CI, 6.8-49.9%). Adverse events were predominantly grade 1-2; one grade 3 abdominal pain event and no grade 4-5 events were recorded. Only three deaths occurred during a median OS follow-up of 15.6 months, making survival estimates exploratory and statistically immature. Conclusions: In this small, single-center pilot cohort of highly selected patients, EUS-guided intratumoral P-32 microparticle implantation combined with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel was technically feasible and provided preliminary safety information. Because of the absence of a chemotherapy-only comparator, the small sample size, and the limited follow-up, the radiographic, biomarker, resection, and survival outcomes cannot be attributed specifically to P-32 implantation and should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are required to determine clinical efficacy.

papers.abstract: Distinction of melanoma from less aggressive melanocytic neoplasms is essential to avoid over- or undertreatment. Melanocytic neoplasms can harbor a broad spectrum of molecular drivers, including mutations, amplifications, and fusions, associated with an array of morphologies and biologic behavior. This molecular complexity creates challenges for classification and diagnosis of malignancy. Here, we review current knowledge to present a molecular framework for classifying melanocytic neoplasia and describe current molecular testing modalities useful for informing accurate diagnosis in challenging cases.

papers.abstract: Prognostic PET biomarkers in glioblastoma remain mostly as a single tracer and poorly characterized at recurrence. We investigated whether paired [18F]FDOPA/[18F]FDG PET captures complementary metabolic information associated with survival in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Sixty-five consecutive patients underwent paired [18F]FDOPA/[18F]FDG PET/MR at baseline and/or recurrence. Survival was analyzed from baseline PET/MR (OS1, n = 36) and recurrence PET/MR (OS2, n = 55); longitudinal analyses used the paired subgroup (n = 26). FDOPA and FDG tumor masks were independently segmented within a FLAIR-derived tumor box, and metrics were extracted from tracer-specific masks, their intersection, and their union. Metrics significant in Kaplan-Meier or univariable Cox analyses were tested in adjusted Cox models. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was used as a sensitivity analysis for the continuous Cox screening tests. In exploratory screening, prognostic associations were sparse at baseline and more prominent at recurrence. At OS2, three metrics remained independently associated with survival after adjustment: the FDOPA/FDG union-domain SUVmeanunion ratio (HR, 1.50; p = 0.0168), MTVinter (HR, 1.63; p = 0.0154), and MTVDOPA (HR, 1.58; p = 0.0191). The SUVmeanunion ratio and MTVDOPA showed limited correlation, suggesting complementary information. Their integration into IR-MTVDOPA, defined as FDOPA/FDG SUVmeanunion ratio × log(MTVDOPA), showed higher apparent OS2 discrimination (HR, 1.73; log-rank p = 0.0001; C-index, 0.730; bootstrap .632-corrected C-index, 0.684; 12-month AUC, 0.863). In this exploratory single-center cohort, paired [18F]FDOPA/[18F]FDG PET showed prognostic associations at recurrence. Inter-tracer intensity balance and metabolic tumor burden provided partially complementary survival information, and their exploratory integration showed higher apparent discrimination. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Liver transplantation may provide prolonged survival in fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC), but the frequency and timing of post-transplant recurrence, and the basis for patient selection, remain poorly defined. We described the course from listing through long-term follow-up and tested whether routine pretransplant measurements distinguished the recurrence risk. Methods: Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients data identified separate listing and first-transplant cohorts during 2002-2025. Competing-risk analyses assessed waiting-list outcomes and reported recurrence of the pretransplant tumour. Exploratory recurrence models were internally validated with 500 patient bootstrap samples, with performance assessed only in omitted recipients. Recorded explant tumour extent was examined in the registry's liver explant file. Results: This study included 61 listed candidates and 51 first-transplant recipients; 42 recipients had a pathology-supported discharge diagnosis of FLC. One-year incidence of transplantation was 76.5% (95% CI 65.9-86.6). After a median potential follow-up of 8.1 years, five-year post-transplant survival was 63.3% (95% CI 46.4-76.2). Seventeen recurrences were reported and the three-year cumulative incidence was 26.1% (95% CI 13.9-39.1). Malignancy was the recorded primary cause in 13 of 23 deaths. Laboratory-component and compact clinical models had mean three-year validation areas under the curve of 0.571 and 0.507, and neither reduced prediction error relative to its matched cohort-average prediction. Conclusions: Transplantation was followed by prolonged survival in selected patients with FLC, although reported recurrence was common and sometimes late. Routine pretransplant variables did not identify reproducible recurrence-risk groups. With 51 recipients and 17 recurrences, these estimates are imprecise and the prediction analyses are exploratory; selection should remain multidisciplinary while tumour extent, treatment response and biological markers are evaluated prospectively.

papers.abstract: Sleeve lobectomy serves as a parenchyma-sparing alternative to pneumonectomy for central non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study describes and compares early postoperative outcomes and overall survival between sleeve lobectomy and pneumonectomy and explores factors associated with survival. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on 97 consecutive patients with central NSCLC operated at the Marius Nasta National Institute of Pneumophthisiology between September 2021 and December 2022, with follow-up through 1 March 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: sleeve lobectomy (n = 41) and pneumonectomy (n = 56). Early morbidity, mortality, and overall survival were evaluated using univariate analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. After multivariable adjustment, surgical procedure was not significantly associated with overall survival. A low rate of major anastomotic complications was observed in the sleeve lobectomy group, with one case of early partial anastomotic leak (2.44%) requiring surgical reinforcement. In an exploratory multivariable model, pathological nodal involvement and the number of involved lymph nodes were associated with mortality. In appropriately selected patients where an R0 parenchyma-sparing resection is technically feasible, sleeve lobectomy is associated with acceptable morbidity and survival. After adjustment, the surgical procedure was not significantly associated with overall survival. Nodal disease burden was the factor most strongly associated with survival in this cohort.

papers.abstract: Background: Kidney tumors comprise a biologically diverse and diagnostically challenging group of neoplasms. Many entities share overlapping morphologic features despite having distinct molecular profiles. Although histomorphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular biomarker testing has become increasingly important for accurate classification, recognition of emerging entities, identification of hereditary cancer syndromes, and therapeutic decision-making. Focus of the Review: This narrative review provides a practical, pathology-oriented framework for molecular biomarker testing in kidney tumors. It integrates immunohistochemistry, fluorescence in situ hybridization, polymerase chain reaction-based methods, and next-generation sequencing with morphologic assessment. Particular attention is given to diagnostically relevant alterations involving VHL, TFE3, TFEB, MET, FH, ELOC, and ALK, genes encoding SDH subunits, and components of the mTOR signaling pathway, together with commonly used immunohistochemical surrogates. The prognostic and predictive roles of selected biomarkers, including their potential value in hereditary risk assessment and treatment selection, are also discussed. Practical limitations, such as limited biopsy material, intratumoral heterogeneity, and technical variability, are considered. Conclusions: Molecular biomarker testing is reshaping kidney tumor pathology by supporting an integrated diagnostic approach that complements, rather than replaces, careful morphologic evaluation. Its appropriate use can improve diagnostic accuracy, refine clinical stratification, and facilitate the recognition of emerging renal tumor entities with hereditary or therapeutic relevance. Future developments are expected to include methylation profiling, transcriptomic classifiers, liquid biopsy platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Arterial coupling in microsurgery remains technically challenging despite widespread venous coupler adoption. We developed a novel everter device to facilitate arterial anastomosis using mechanical couplers and evaluated its feasibility and potential efficiency in abdominal-based breast reconstruction. Methods: Five pigs underwent paired superior epigastric artery flap reconstruction with everter-assisted and hand-sewn arterial anastomoses, analyzed using a paired t-test. A retrospective clinical series included 12 patients, 22 reconstructed breasts, 14 coupling attempts, and 8 primary hand-sewn recipient arterial anastomoses. The primary clinical outcome was successful coupling without revision or conversion. Clinical timing comparisons were descriptive. Results: All five porcine arterial couplings were successful. Mean arterial time was 8.47 ± 2.83 min versus 20.26 ± 3.32 min for hand-sewn controls, a paired reduction of 11.79 min (95% CI, 5.86 to 17.72; p = 0.005). Clinical coupling succeeded in 9 of 14 attempts (64.3%). Five attempts required conversion (35.7%), including three thrombotic and two technical failures. All were converted intraoperatively, with no flap loss. Mean arterial times were 9.2 ± 4.2 min for successful coupling (n = 8) and 20.2 ± 8.0 min for primary hand-sewn anastomosis (n = 6), an approximately 55% difference. Conclusions: Everter-assisted arterial coupling demonstrated clinical feasibility and shorter mean arterial times when successfully completed. These findings support further refinement and evaluation of the technique to establish safety and overall procedural efficiency.

papers.abstract: Background: This exploratory study assessed whether qualitative dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) time-intensity curves (TICs) differentiate non-progressive treatment-related changes (NPTRC) from tumor progression after stereotactic radiotherapy for brain metastases. Methods: Thirty-two patients with 51 treated lesions underwent DCE-MRI. Five neuroradiologists independently delineated a volume of interest and classified the resulting TIC as Type A-D. Longitudinal clinical and MRI follow-up provided the reference outcome, which was recorded before the TIC framework was finalized. An A/B versus C/D grouping was evaluated as a secondary exploratory analysis. Results: Thirty-five lesions were classified as NPTRC and 16 as tumor progression. All 17 Type A lesions were NPTRC, whereas all 13 Type C/D lesions showed progression. Type B was observed in 21 of 51 lesions (41.2%), including 18 NPTRC and 3 progressive lesions, representing a substantial indeterminate subgroup. The exploratory A/B versus C/D grouping yielded 81.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The ordinal TIC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.952. Interobserver agreement was high within the present reader group (Fleiss' κ = 0.889). Conclusions: Type A was associated with NPTRC, Types C/D were associated with progression, and Type B represented an indeterminate pattern. These descriptive findings require independent validation before clinical use.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: During radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), electrodes are generally inserted into the center of the tumor through the hepatic parenchyma under image guidance, including ultrasound or computed tomography (CT) guidance. However, tumors located just below the hepatic capsule require special puncture techniques. This retrospective study aimed to analyze the efficacy and outcomes of RFA for HCC located just below the subcapsular region of the liver. Methods: A total of 81 patients with 81 subcapsular HCC tumors underwent RFA. Baseline patient characteristics, treatment results, and adverse events were investigated. Factors associated with local recurrence were also examined. Results: Among the 81 patients, 59 (73%) were male, the median age was 74 years (range, 46-93 years), and 68 (84%) were classified as Child-Pugh class A. The median tumor size was 1.5 cm (range, 0.5-3.7 cm), and 56 of 81 tumors (69%) were <2.0 cm in diameter. 53 tumors were located in the right lobe of the liver (65%). Monopolar RFA was performed in 55 patients (68%), and no-touch multi-bipolar RFA was performed in 26 patients (32%). Treatment success was achieved in 75 tumors (93%), with inadequate ablative margins observed in 6 tumors (7%). Of these six tumors, five (83%) were treated with monopolar RFA; however, differences between the RFA devices were not statistically significant (p = 0.368). Local tumor progression (LTP) was observed in 19 patients (24%), with cumulative LTP rates of 13%, 29%, 33%, and 33% at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. Multivariate analysis using a COX proportional hazards model identified insufficient ablative margins as a significant factor associated with LTP (hazard ratio, 4.64; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-14.9; p = 0.031). Adverse events occurred in 17 patients (21%), all of whom recovered with conservative treatment. Tumor seeding occurred in only one patient (1%). Conclusions: In the present study, achieving an adequate ablative margin using either monopolar or multi-bipolar RFA systems was associated with a reduced risk of local tumor recurrence in patients with subcapsular HCC.

papers.abstract: The imaging-defined peritumoral region may contain quantitative imaging information beyond that captured by the tumor core, but its radiomic deviation from normal-appearing breast parenchyma remains insufficiently characterized. This retrospective single-center study investigated whether peritumoral-to-normal radiomic distances exceed the within-patient bilateral normal-appearing parenchymal reference distance. Fifty-six patients with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer and preoperative bilateral dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI were included. Single-slice radiomic analysis was performed for four predefined regions: tumor core (T), peritumoral microenvironment (M), remote ipsilateral normal-appearing parenchyma (I), and contralateral normal-appearing parenchyma (C). After quality control, 101 radiomic features were standardized and analyzed using standardized Euclidean, Manhattan, cosine, and Ledoit-Wolf Mahalanobis distances. Peritumoral-to-ipsilateral (dMI) and peritumoral-to-contralateral (dMC) distances were compared with the within-patient bilateral normal-appearing parenchymal distance (dIC). Across all four metrics, both dMI and dMC exceeded dIC, and all eight primary paired Wilcoxon comparisons remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (q≤1.07×10-6), with matched-pairs rank-biserial correlations ranging from 0.749 to 0.989. The principal pattern was broadly preserved across alternative Mahalanobis covariance formulations, reduced-dimensional PCA analyses, particularly when three or four principal components were retained, exclusion of all 13 retained shape features, separate radiomic feature-family analyses, and replacement of selected non-normalized non-uniformity features with normalized counterparts. These findings show that, in the present cohort, peritumoral-to-normal radiomic distances exceeded the within-patient bilateral normal-appearing parenchymal reference distance. Because the four analyzed regions differed in size, shape, and sampling geometry, the reported distances should be interpreted as region-level radiomic differences under the present ROI definitions rather than as geometry-independent tissue properties. Larger multi-institutional studies using full-volume three-dimensional radiomics and standardized imaging and preprocessing strategies are needed to assess reproducibility, clarify the biological correlates of this radiomic pattern, and evaluate its potential clinical relevance.

papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy is an emerging approach for the molecular characterization of hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) malignancies through the analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and extracellular vesicles (EVs). These biomarkers may complement conventional imaging and serum markers by providing additional information on tumor biology and disease evolution. This narrative review examines the available evidence concerning the potential applications of liquid biopsy in HPB surgical practice, with particular emphasis on preoperative prognostic assessment, postoperative molecular residual disease detection, recurrence monitoring, and treatment adaptation. Among the different circulating biomarkers, ctDNA currently has the most developed perioperative evidence base. Studies involving pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and biliary tract cancers have demonstrated associations between ctDNA detection and unfavorable oncological outcomes, particularly postoperative recurrence. Nevertheless, the available evidence remains predominantly observational, with considerable heterogeneity in patient populations, sampling protocols, analytical platforms, and outcome definitions. Although the integration of circulating biomarkers with conventional anatomical criteria has generated interest in the concept of "biological resectability", this framework remains hypothetical and has not been prospectively validated for surgical treatment selection. Similarly, ctDNA-guided modifications of neoadjuvant therapy, adjuvant treatment, or postoperative surveillance have not yet demonstrated clinical benefit in HPB malignancies. Liquid biopsy should therefore currently be regarded as a promising investigational prognostic tool rather than an established determinant of surgical or oncological management. Standardized methodologies and prospective interventional trials are required before its routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pathological response to neoadjuvant treatment in rectal cancer may differ between the primary tumor and regional lymph nodes, and the prognostic implications of this discordance remain incompletely defined. We evaluated oncological outcomes according to combined pathological tumor-nodal response patterns, with particular emphasis on complete primary-tumor regression with residual ypN-positive disease. Methods: A total of 215 patients with nonmetastatic rectal adenocarcinoma who received neoadjuvant treatment followed by curative-intent resection were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified as ypT0N0 (n = 34), ypT0N+ (n = 13), residual primary tumor/ypN0 (n = 119), or residual primary tumor/ypN+ (n = 49). The primary endpoint was time to recurrence (TTR). Kaplan-Meier, Cox, Firth penalized Cox, competing-risk, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: Median follow-up was 70.0 months. Recurrence occurred in 2/34 (5.9%), 6/13 (46.2%), 17/119 (14.3%), and 18/49 (36.7%) patients, respectively. Estimated 5-year recurrence-free probabilities were 90.1%, 53.8%, 81.6%, and 46.3%, respectively (log-rank p < 0.0001). Compared with ypT0N0, recurrence hazard was significantly higher for ypT0N+ (adjusted hazard ratio 7.56, 95% confidence interval 1.49-38.40; p = 0.015) and residual primary tumor/ypN+ (adjusted hazard ratio 7.10, 95% confidence interval 1.64-30.83; p = 0.009). In an analysis restricted to patients with baseline cT3N1 disease, the association for ypT0N+ remained evident (adjusted hazard ratio 6.34, 95% confidence interval 1.19-33.79; p = 0.031). Competing-risk analyses were concordant, and all documented recurrences in the ypT0N+ group involved distant metastasis. Conclusions: In this cohort, residual ypN-positive disease despite complete pathological regression of the primary tumor was associated with an increased risk of recurrence. Given the small number of patients with ypT0N+ disease, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract: Background: The four molecular subtypes of endometrial carcinoma defined by The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) can be reconstructed from multi-omics data, but these data contain about 460,000 features for 369 patients, the subtypes are imbalanced, and feature selection easily leaks test-set information. Methods: We developed POISE-X, a leakage-controlled, imbalance-aware benchmarking pipeline with an interchangeable metaheuristic search engine. Using RNA-seq, miRNA, DNA methylation, copy-number, mutation, and clinical data from 369 TCGA-UCEC patients, we compared 19 optimizers under nested five-fold cross-validation, with in-fold prefiltering to 2505 candidate features and a macro-averaged F1 fitness function. Results: Performance differed across optimizers in a Friedman test on fold means (p=1.989×10-6). No selected panel exceeded logistic regression on the full candidate pool, which reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.902; the compact configuration chosen by our selection rule, POISE-GWO, retained 443 features with a macro-averaged F1 of 0.880, and the selection rule itself scored 0.881 under leave-one-fold-out evaluation, and an ANOVA-ranked panel of 450 features reached 0.886. These results held without clinical variables and, in the two searches tested, for parsimony weights of 0.8-0.99. A surrogate of the clinical molecular classification built from POLE exonuclease-domain mutation, mismatch-repair deficiency, and TP53 mutation reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.924, higher on average than every multi-omics model. Conclusions: In this cohort, wrapper search therefore compressed the feature set without adding discriminative power, and the selected panels reconstructed an existing classification, not a new treatment-relevant signature. POISE-X is a framework for benchmarking feature-selection strategies; any selected panel requires external validation before clinical use.

papers.abstract: Aim: Estrone (E1) is of particular interest as most breast cancers are diagnosed after menopause, the period in which E1 becomes the dominant estrogen. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly invasive cancer that lacks hormone receptors for estrogen (ER), progesterone (PR), and HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor-2). TNBC management remains clinically challenging despite recent advances in targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches. This study investigated the effects of the estrogen hormone estrone sulfate (E1S) on cancer cells. Here, E1S engages in non-classical biased G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) signaling in TNBC MDA-MB-231 cells, estrogen receptor-positive MCF-7 breast cancer cells, and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells, which express estrogen, progesterone, and androgen receptors. Methods: We performed sialidase and colocalization assays in breast MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells. An epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) transition, a tunneling nanotube assay, and a scratch wound assay were conducted to elucidate the cellular behaviors of E1S. We used a RawBlue reporter macrophage cell line to measure NFκB activity using the secreted embryonic alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) assay, and we measured cellular viability and metabolic activity using the AlamarBlue assay. Results: E1S induced NMBR/MMP9/Neu1 signaling in MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, PANC-1 and RawBlue cells. E1S increased E-cadherin expression, reduced N-cadherin and vimentin expression, decreased tunneling nanotube density, and reduced scratch wound migration. E1S increased SEAP activity, suggestive of increased nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and activator protein-1 (AP-1)-mediated transcription. E1S treatment did not affect cell viability and metabolic activity in triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cells using the AlamarBlue assay in a dose-dependent manner. Conclusions: E1S binding to GPER potentiates a biased heterodimerization with the GPCR neuromedin B receptor (NMBR) to activate matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9) and neuraminidase 1 (Neu1), a signaling paradigm with previously established receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) and Toll-like (TLR) receptors. Biased, temporal GPER signaling has significant implications for breast and pancreatic cancer cellular behavior, which may be leveraged to inform therapeutic strategies for aggressive forms of breast and pancreatic cancers. This research study is mechanistic in nature and may have potential translational implications.

papers.abstract: Background: Accurate evaluation of bone marrow involvement is important for staging and treatment monitoring in pediatric neuroblastoma. This study evaluated flow cytometry for detecting neuroblastoma cells in bone marrow aspirates. Methods: In this prospective exploratory correlative analysis, samples from 28 children were assessed through flow cytometry and cytomorphology; available histopathological and iodine-123 metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy results were compared. Neuroblastoma cells were identified as nucleated CD56+CD45-CD36-CD71- events. Results: Flow cytometry detected neuroblastoma cell populations across a broad quantitative range, including low-level populations. Agreement between flow cytometry and cytomorphology was 90.0% (Cohen's κ = 0.56). In 16 paired aspirate-level records with at least one positive result, flow cytometric and cytomorphological percentages showed a positive Pearson correlation (r = 0.878, p < 0.0001), although this association was sensitive to one high-value observation. Agreement with histopathology was 92.1-94.8% (κ = 0.59-0.64), whereas agreement with MIBG scintigraphy was slight to fair (κ = 0.12-0.23). Conclusions: Flow cytometry provided rapid, quantitative detection of neuroblastoma cell populations in bone marrow aspirates. It should be considered complementary to cytomorphology and histopathology, as repeated examinations, the limited panel, and the lack of an independent reference standard preclude definitive estimates of diagnostic performance.

papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) remains a leading cause of cancer death in Chilean women. Gallstones are present in >90% of GBC cases, but few individuals with gallstones develop cancer, suggesting additional factors are needed. To determine whether obesity increases the risk of progression from gallstones to high-grade dysplasia (HGD) and GBC, we used data from the Chile Biliary Longitudinal Study, 2016-2025, comprising women with ultrasound-detected gallstones in high-incidence regions of Chile.We measured body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) at baseline and up to two follow-up visits. We used Cox proportional-hazards models with age as the time scale to quantify associations of time-varying BMI and WHtR with HGD/GBC risk. During a median follow-up of 4.8 years, 116 of 4711 women developed HGD/GBC. Time-varying BMI was not significantly associated with HGD/GBC risk (p-overall = 0.11; p-nonlinearity = 0.20). In contrast, time-varying WHtR showed a non-linear association with HGD/GBC (p-overall = 0.02; p-nonlinearity = 0.02). Baseline WHtR and BMI models showed similar patterns of associations. Based on longitudinal WHtR trajectories among cases and lag sensitivity analyses, preclinical disease-related weight loss is unlikely to fully explain the observed associations. In conclusion, central obesity measured by WHtR was non-linearly associated with HGD/GBC risk in this population, suggesting that central adiposity may impact the progression from gallstones to HGD/GBC.

papers.abstract: The efficacy of somatostatin analogues (SSA) in Grade 3 (G3) neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) remains controversial, and registry data rarely permit a formal separation of NET G3 from neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC). We analyzed 519 patients with G3 gastroenteropancreatic (GEP) NEN recorded in a national neuroendocrine tumor registry (data export 3 April 2025; 464 de novo G3, 55 transformed G3); bronchopulmonary primaries were excluded. A Ki-67 > 55%, entered as a time-varying indicator, served as a surrogate for NEC. Outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models with all treatments and the Ki-67 > 55% indicator entered as time-varying covariates. Among 410 patients with classifiable Ki-67, 256 (62.4%) ever had a Ki-67 > 55%. Ki-67 > 55% was associated with worse progression-free survival (PFS; HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.06-1.84; p = 0.016) and overall survival (OS; HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; p = 0.006). SSA use was not significantly associated with PFS (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.85-2.04; p = 0.215) or OS (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.54-1.56; p = 0.744). After adjustment for Ki-67, transformed G3 was associated with worse OS (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.02-2.51; p = 0.040). SSA therapy was not associated with improved survival in G3 GEP-NEN. As this is an observational analysis subject to confounding by indication, these estimates do not establish a lack of biological efficacy of SSA. A Ki-67 threshold of 55% identified a prognostically distinct subgroup and explains why transformed G3 appears indolent: after adjustment, it was associated with worse overall survival. This finding rests on 55 patients with 29 deaths and is hypothesis-generating.

papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent form of RCC and is defined by loss of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) function and dysregulated hypoxia signaling. Hyperactivation of the mTOR pathway is also frequently observed. These factors increase anabolic and protein-synthetic demand leading to proteotoxic stress. To survive under these conditions, ccRCC cells rely on adaptive endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress responses and autophagy to maintain proteostasis. Regulated in Development and DNA Damage Response 1 (REDD1, also known as DDIT4) is a key stress response protein that integrates hypoxic, metabolic, and ER stress signals to regulate mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) complex 1 (mTORC1) activity and redox homeostasis. REDD1 can either suppress tumor growth through mTOR inhibition or promote survival by facilitating oxidative stress tolerance and autophagy depending on the specific context. In ccRCC, REDD1 expression is driven by VHL loss and HIF stabilization. Yet, mTORC1 activity frequently persists due to dysregulation of upstream repressors such as TSC1/TSC2, direct activating mutations in mTOR, and enhanced growth factor signaling. This paradox underscores the complex interplay between REDD1 and the oncogenic signaling landscape of RCC. Here, we review emerging evidence positioning REDD1 as a pivotal link between hypoxia, mTOR signaling, and ER stress in ccRCC and discuss how therapeutic modulation of this pathway through ER stress inducers, proteasome inhibitors, and p97/valosin-containing protein (VCP) inhibitors may overcome adaptive resistance and improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: We evaluated molecular selection stability and external prediction beyond age, sex and broad pathological stage in resected stage I-II lung adenocarcinoma. Models were developed in 228 patients from two sources and frozen before evaluation in four historical cohorts containing 778 patients. The primary comparison added pathway scores using elastic-net Cox regression. Secondary analyses examined a gene model, 200 development bootstrap resamples, alternative modeling specifications and locally updated baselines. Prediction error was measured by the integrated Brier score over 1-3 years (IBS); negative molecular-minus-clinical differences (ΔIBS) favored molecular models. Evaluation intervals used 2000 paired bootstrap resamples. The pathway model retained no molecular terms. The final gene model retained 16 genes, whereas both source-held-out fits and 159/200 development resamples retained none. Penalties of 0.5, 0.15 and 0.05 were selected in 160, 38 and 2 resamples. Alternative specifications changed gene retention from 0 to 61 and pathway retention from 0 to 5. Frozen gene-model ΔIBS ranged from -0.0034 to 0.0055 across cohorts. Its equal cohort mean was 0.0016 (95% CI, -0.0012 to 0.0042), compared with -0.0008 (-0.0024 to 0.0007) after cross-fitted local baseline updating. The clinical model predicted a 3-year mortality of 19.6% in Japan and 22.6% in Moffitt, versus observed values of 9.1% and 28.6%. Molecular selection was unstable, and incremental performance depended on specification and population. The results characterize these learning procedures and their limited development sample; broader transcriptomic prognostic value and contemporary clinical utility remain unestablished.

papers.abstract: Architectural innovation is widely assumed to improve the cross-institutional generalization of tumor segmentation models, yet this is rarely tested. We compared three architectural families under an identical, leak-safe protocol in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) segmentation. Convolutional (nnU-Net ResEnc-M), state-space (U-Mamba Bot) and transformer (SwinUNETR) models were trained on HCC-TACE-Seg (n = 103) with identical patient-disjoint five-fold splits, then applied without adaptation to 3D-IRCADb (n = 15) and LiTS (n = 118). We assessed discrimination, case-level failure concordance, lesion-volume dependence, calibration and selective prediction. Internal performance differed (Dice 0.685, 0.662, 0.479; Friedman p = 0.022) but external performance was low and largely convergent: the convolutional and state-space models were formally equivalent on both external cohorts (pre-specified margin ±0.05 Dice), whereas the transformer was inferior on LiTS (0.222; p < 0.0001) and inconclusive on 3D-IRCADb. Case-level Dice was highly concordant across all pairings (Spearman ρ = 0.84-0.96; 0.67-0.81 on LiTS after adjustment for lesion volume), the same cases failing across architectures. Lesion volume predicted performance in all six architecture × cohort combinations; lesions < 5 mL failed completely in 61-76% of cases and formed 1.9% of the development cohort against 31.4% of LiTS. Neither liver-mask constraint nor ensembling recovered performance. Deferring the 30% least-confident LiTS cases raised Dice to 0.516 (0.450 when only empty predictions were removed). Under a single-source, TACE-treated HCC training regime, cross-dataset failure of liver-tumor segmentation was governed primarily by lesion size rather than by architectural family; confidence-based selective prediction offers a deployable mitigation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sustained drug-free status is an emerging milestone after atezolizumab plus bevacizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. We examined baseline host biomarkers associated with achievement of 6-month sustained drug-free status and evaluated a composite stratification score. Methods: This multicentre retrospective study included patients treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. The endpoint required systemic therapy discontinuation after complete response or no viable disease, followed by at least 6 months without viable or recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma and sustained normalization of initially elevated tumour markers. The PAN-DF score (preserved hepatic reserve, altered immune-inflammatory status, and nutritional-immune reserve for achieving drug-free status) combined modified albumin-bilirubin grade, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and prognostic nutritional index. Results: Among 655 patients, 25 achieved the endpoint; median post-discontinuation follow-up was 533 days. In the complete-case cohort (n = 473; 17 events), achievement rates were 0.0%, 2.9%, 3.7%, and 13.6% for scores 0-3. Each one-point increase was associated with higher odds of achievement (odds ratio 2.90, 95% confidence interval 1.51-5.55; p = 0.001), and the area under the curve was 0.719. The examined baseline tumour-related factors were not significantly associated with the primary endpoint, and the examined host-related factors were not associated with objective response. Conclusions: Selected baseline host biomarkers were associated with achievement of 6-month sustained drug-free status. PAN-DF stratified the observed probability of this outcome and may help identify patient groups with a relatively higher likelihood of a sustained drug-free state, supporting early multidisciplinary planning.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pericardial effusion may occur in patients with established cancer but may also represent the first manifestation of an occult malignancy. This study evaluated the diagnostic contribution of pericardial fluid cytology and pathological assessment according to previous oncological status, with particular emphasis on previously unrecognized malignancy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients hospitalized with pericardial disease between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary cardiovascular center. The final cohort comprised 234 clinical episodes in 209 patients. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, procedural, cytological, and histopathological data were analyzed in relation to previous oncological status and malignant pericardial involvement. Results: Pathological assessment was available in 95/234 episodes (40.6%), with neoplastic involvement identified in 21/95 (22.1%). Neoplastic findings occurred in 13/33 (39.4%) evaluable episodes with known malignancy and 8/62 (12.9%) without a previous cancer diagnosis (odds ratio, 4.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.59-12.11; p = 0.004). Conversely, 20/33 (60.6%) evaluable episodes in patients with known cancer showed no neoplastic involvement. In all eight patients without previously known malignancy, pericardial fluid cytology provided the first pathological evidence of cancer; six (75%) had findings suggestive of a pulmonary origin. All presented with large effusions and hemodynamic compromise. Conclusions: Pericardial pathological assessment provides diagnostic information beyond previous oncological status. It can distinguish malignant from non-neoplastic pericardial involvement in patients with established cancer while also revealing occult malignancy when pericardial disease is its first presentation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy is usually attributed to DNA repair, drug efflux and apoptotic threshold. Chloride channels intersect these processes but are rarely considered as a group. This review asks whether chloride flux forms a coherent, targetable axis of treatment response and, if not, how the therapeutic direction differs by channel and tissue. Methods: PubMed was searched to 23 August 2026; all free-text searches were re-executed on 22 September 2026 and supplemented by controlled-vocabulary searches. Cited records were checked against NCBI E-utilities and screened for retractions. Claims were graded by whether pharmacological phenotypes were reproduced by genetic perturbation and by the available target-engagement and replication evidence. Results: The therapeutic direction is not uniform. In experimental models, LRRC8A- and LRRC8D-containing channels mediate substantial platinum uptake, and dose-stratified associations between their expression and outcome have been reported in head and neck cancer, supporting prospective evaluation as predictive biomarkers; contrary reports in ovarian, colon and breast models indicate that this direction is established for platinum uptake rather than for cytotoxic resistance in general. CFTR is an intestinal tumour suppressor and the only channel reviewed with an approved potentiator, yet its direction reverses in glioma, with a prostate report of CFTR-dependent cisplatin resistance pointing in the same direction. Conversely, ClC-3, ANO1 and CLIC1 are associated with resistance when gained, although CLIC1 is better supported as a determinant of drug response than of tumorigenesis. Sixteen modulators are compared by potency, assay format, selectivity/counter-screening and clinical status; widely used blockers are often poorly selective. Conclusions: Chloride transport is not a single therapeutic target class. Candidate chloride-channel blockers should be counter-screened against LRRC8/VRAC before combination with platinum therapy, and CFTR potentiation should not be generalised across tumour types. Conflicting evidence is reported alongside the directions it qualifies rather than set aside.

papers.title: Chloride Channels as Determinants of Anti-Cancer Drug Response: Why the Therapeutic Direction Reverses Between Channels and Between Tissues.

papers.abstract: Objective: To compare survival of patients with different histological types of locally advanced cervical cancer after treatment with radical surgery or radical radiotherapy. Methods: Data for United States residents diagnosed with locally advanced cervical cancer between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. Overall survival and cancer-specific survival were compared using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. To minimize baseline differences, patients from each group were paired using propensity score matching. Results: Among the 1,363 patients with squamous cell carcinoma in the propensity score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival when disease was in stage IB3 (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.97), but not when it was in other stages. Cancer-specific survival did not differ significantly between the two treatments at any disease stage. Among the 576 patients with adenocarcinoma in the propensity-score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival in stages IB3 (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.28-0.77) or IIA2 (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.96) or IIB involving tumors < 4 cm (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.16-0.80). It was also associated with significantly better cancer-specific survival in stages IB3 (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29-0.90), IIA2 (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.76) or IIB involving tumors < 4 cm (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.07-0.62). Conclusions: Surgery may be associated with better overall survival than radiotherapy in stage IB3 squamous cell carcinoma. In the case of adenocarcinoma, surgery may be associated with better overall and cancer-specific survival than radiotherapy in stage IB3 or IIA2 and in stage IIB involving tumors < 4 cm.

papers.abstract: EGFR-TKIs serve as standard first-line targeted therapy for EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Real-world data on the prognostic role of baseline HBsAg positivity and the risk of HBV reactivation during EGFR-TKI treatment remain limited, particularly in HBV-endemic Chinese populations. This retrospective single-center cohort study enrolled 580 consecutive patients with stage III-IV EGFR-mutant LUAD who received EGFR-TKIs between 2013 and 2026. Patients were grouped by baseline HBsAg status; Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox models adjusted for key clinical covariates were used to evaluate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). HBV reactivation was defined by EASL criteria, with virological evaluation available for 51 of 82 HBsAg-positive patients. Among all enrolled patients, 14.1% were HBsAg-positive. The HBV reactivation rate was 9.8% among evaluable HBsAg-positive patients, and reactivation was not independently linked to survival. After adjustment, baseline HBsAg positivity showed a borderline trend toward poorer OS (HR = 1.42, 95% CI, 0.99-2.04, p = 0.054) without significant PFS association (HR = 1.14, 95% CI, 0.80-1.62, p = 0.481). Liver metastasis independently predicted worse OS in HBsAg-positive patients (HR = 3.84, 95% CI, 1.65-8.94, p = 0.002). HBV reactivation was uncommon but warrants close monitoring during EGFR-TKI therapy. Baseline HBsAg positivity demonstrated only a non-significant trend toward inferior OS without affecting PFS. Routine HBsAg screening at diagnosis may facilitate risk stratification, and HBsAg-positive patients with liver metastasis require intensified surveillance.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Longitudinal monitoring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy primarily focuses on CAR-T-cell expansion. However, comprehensive immunophenotypic characterization of both CAR-T and endogenous T cells remains limited. We investigated longitudinal immune dynamics following tisagenlecleucel treatment using multiparameter flow cytometry. Methods: Nineteen patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies (11 diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and eight B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia) receiving tisagenlecleucel were prospectively enrolled. Serial peripheral blood samples collected during the first 28 days after infusion were analyzed for CAR-T-cell kinetics, differentiation status, activation and exhaustion marker expression, longitudinal phenotypic changes, as well as associations with treatment response and immune-related toxicities. Results: CAR-T-cell expansion predominantly peaked on day 7 after infusion. However, in several patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, delayed peak expansion was observed. At peak expansion, CAR-T-cells were enriched for a central memory phenotype and exhibited significantly higher HLA-DR and PD-1 expression than endogenous T cells. During follow-up, the proportion of central memory T-cells progressively declined, whereas the proportion of terminal effector T-cells increased, which was accompanied by reduced expression of HLA-DR, PD-1, and TIGIT. Despite the distinct activation profiles, CAR-T and endogenous T-cells displayed broadly similar differentiation patterns. Exploratory analyses further demonstrated higher absolute CAR-T-cell counts in patients who developed immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome. Conclusions: This clinically applicable approach provides immunophenotypic information beyond CAR-T-cell enumeration alone and may facilitate biomarker discovery and longitudinal immune monitoring in patients receiving CAR-T-cell therapy.
