papers.abstract: ZNFX1 is an RNA helicase that plays a critical role in host defense against viral infections. Recent studies further revealed that ZNFX1 harbors an unexpected RNA-ubiquitinating E3 ligase activity, raising fundamental questions about how RNA-binding activates this multifunctional enzyme. Here, we combine cryo-electron microscopy with biochemical analyses to define the structural basis of ZNFX1 regulation. In the absence of RNA, ZNFX1 adopts an autoinhibited conformation in which a blocking helix occludes the RNA-binding groove. It exists predominantly as autoinhibited monomers, and, at higher concentrations, assembles into short helical filaments composed of repeating tetramers. Binding of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) remodels these higher-order assemblies into RNA-bound ZNFX1 monomers and dimers. The cryo-EM structure of the ssRNA-bound ZNFX1 dimer reveals that RNA binding displaces the blocking helix and induces large-scale conformational rearrangements that remodel the helicase core into an active configuration. Biochemical analyses validate the proposed RNA-binding interfaces and demonstrate ATP-dependent RNA unwinding by ZNFX1. Together, these findings support a regulatory mechanism in which autoinhibited ZNFX1 exists as monomers or concentration-dependent higher-order oligomers, whereas RNA binding promotes structural remodeling and helicase activation.

papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis and complex tumour microenvironment. We previously demonstrated that doublecortin-like kinase 1 (DCLK1) is associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in CCA; however, its biological functions and clinical relevance remain unclear. Herein, we elucidated the role of DCLK1 in CCA progression, focusing on its effects on angiogenesis, and evaluated its potential as a prognostic marker. We analysed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data to characterise DCLK1 expression and function in CCA. Functional validation was performed using conditioned medium from DCLK1-modified CCA cells, as well as endothelial tube formation, migration, and invasion assays. Tumour vascular density was assessed using a xenograft model. We used a human angiogenesis-related antibody array, western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and nuclear translocation assays to examine CXCL5 expression and NF-κB pathway activity. We found that DCLK1 was upregulated in CCA and correlated with advanced disease and poor survival. DCLK1⁺ malignant cells displayed pro-angiogenic features and increased paracrine interaction with endothelial cells. Conditioned medium from DCLK1-overexpressing tumour cells enhanced endothelial tube formation, migration, and invasion, whereas DCLK1 knockout reversed these effects. DCLK1-expressing tumours showed increased vascular density in vivo. Mechanistically, an angiogenesis antibody array and western blotting demonstrated that DCLK1 activated the NF-κB pathway to upregulate CXCL5 expression. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB or neutralization of CXCL5 significantly attenuated DCLK1-related pro-angiogenic responses in vitro. DCLK1 activated the NF-κB pathway to upregulate CXCL5 secretion; inhibiting NF-κB or CXCL5 reduced DCLK1-related pro-angiogenic capacity.

papers.abstract: Trace elements including iron, copper, zinc, selenium, and manganese are indispensable for life, serving as enzyme cofactors, structural components, and signaling molecules that govern energy metabolism, redox balance, and genomic stability. Their physiological functions exhibit a characteristic dose-effect biphasicity, wherein homeostatic imbalance can both safeguard health and promote malignant transformation. This review systematically delineates the complete lifecycle of these five core trace elements under physiological conditions, emphasizing their extensive functional interconnections, and elucidates how tumor cells hijack this regulatory network through an element-addiction mechanism. We detail the emerging roles of iron-dependent ferroptosis and copper-dependent cuproptosis, alongside the context-dependent regulation of apoptosis and autophagy by trace elements, revealing tumor-specific metabolic vulnerabilities. Within the tumor immune microenvironment, we examine how zinc, iron, copper, selenium, and manganese function as molecular switches: zinc and selenium generally support antitumor immunity, whereas iron and copper dysregulation drives immunosuppressive polarization; manganese additionally emerges as a cGAS-STING agonist with immunotherapeutic potential. In tumor angiogenesis and metastasis, we explore the central roles of copper and iron in extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and angiogenic signaling. Extensive clinical evidence is integrated to establish systemic and local elemental imbalances as risk biomarkers across diverse cancer types. Therapeutic strategies are categorized into traditional nutritional and pharmacological interventions, element-metabolism-based synergistic sensitization with chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, and interdisciplinary engineering approaches including element-responsive nanoplatforms and synthetic biology-engineered immune cells. Throughout, we emphasize that the majority of therapeutic evidence derives from preclinical models, underscoring that rigorous foundational research must precede clinical translation. We conclude by outlining knowledge gaps and priorities for future investigation, advocating a systems biology framework that acknowledges current limitations while guiding hypothesis-driven exploration.

papers.abstract: Proteomic ageing clocks are emerging tools that estimate biological age from protein abundance patterns. Most models are developed using blood capturing inflammatory, metabolic, and extracellular proteins, including secreted signalling factors. Large-scale plasma studies now predict chronological age, disease risk and mortality, but muscle-related models remain indirect, relying on organ-enriched circulating proteins rather than biopsy-derived skeletal muscle clocks. We review current proteomic clock frameworks, computational approaches, platform considerations and validation strategies, highlighting the potential of muscle-based clocks to capture tissue and subcellular-specific ageing processes. We discuss future integration of spatial, single-cell, and multi-omic data to enhance mechanistic insight and translational relevance.

papers.abstract: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN), a grossly visible precursor of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, is classified into gastric, intestinal, and pancreatobiliary subtypes, each associated with distinct clinicopathological features and biological aggressiveness. We hypothesised that the tumour microenvironment can explain the association between histological subtypes and clinical outcomes. We first enrolled 116 IPMN resection cases, with or without associated invasive carcinoma, and then sequenced four single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) libraries from those with distinct histological grades and subtypes. The snRNA-seq revealed that fibroblasts were the main source of cell-cell communication, whereas myeloid and mast cells were the main receivers. Therefore, we subclassified fibroblasts into inflammatory (iCAF), myofibroblast (myCAF), and reticular-like (rCAF) subpopulations, and myeloid cells into monocytes, neutrophils, macrophages, and dendritic cell subpopulations. Cell-cell interaction analysis revealed that iCAF and rCAF mainly communicated with SPP1High macrophages via the C3-integrin pathway and with neutrophils via the CXCL12-CXCR4 pathway, whereas myCAF mainly communicated with monocytes and mast cells via ECM-related pathways. Subsequently, we performed two panels of Opal multiplex immunohistochemistry and Elastic van Gieson staining to evaluate fibroblast and myeloid subpopulations and collagen, respectively, in all enrolled cases. Quantitative image analyses revealed that iCAF, neutrophils, and SPP1+ macrophages were associated with higher histological grade, whereas myCAF, collagen, monocytes, and mast cells were associated with lower histological grade. No decrease in myCAF or increase in neutrophils was observed in the invasive intestinal type. Finally, we classified the cases into three groups based on the density of fibroblast and myeloid subpopulations: iCAF/SPP1+ macrophage-rich (I-stroma), neutrophil-rich (N-stroma), and myCAF/mast cell-rich (M-stroma). These stromal groups were associated with distinct clinicopathological features. In conclusion, we revealed that the heterogeneous microenvironment of IPMN, associated with distinct clinicopathological features, may explain the clinical significance of histological subtypes. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Children with germline pathogenic variants of DICER1 have a highly elevated risk of cancers in many different organs, recognized as DICER1-related tumor predisposition (DRTP). DRTP tumors/lesions have one inactivated copy and one 'hotspot' mutated copy of DICER1. All 'hotspot' DICER1 mutations impair 5p microRNA (miRNA) production. MiRNAs are short non-coding RNA molecules that downregulate messenger RNA (mRNA) expression. Mature 5p or 3p miRNAs are produced by the endonuclease DICER1. Mature miRNAs are loaded into AGO2-containing RNA-induced silencing complex where they target mRNAs via a seed sequence in the mRNA's 3' untranslated region (3' UTR). Despite evidence of widespread dysregulation of gene expression in the presence of DICER1 'hotspot' mutations, there is no established immunohistochemistry (IHC) marker to complement sequencing-based strategies for identification of DRTP tumors. AGO2 miR-eCLIP and RNA-seq data from a mouse cell model of DRTP (Dicer1E1705K, referred to here as E1705K cells) identified paternally expressed gene 10 (Peg10) as a diagnostic candidate. Peg10 mRNA and protein expression were tested in control and Dicer1-mutant cells, and de-repression of Peg10 3' UTR was tested using reporter assays. PEG10 IHC staining of a human tumor microarray (TMA, n = 63) was performed and the performance of the PEG10 H-score as a DICER1 classifier was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Peg10 mRNA and protein levels were elevated in E1705K cells. Expression of a reporter gene linked to the Peg10 3' UTR was elevated in mutant but not control cells, consistent with altered miRNA regulation of Peg10 in the mutant cells. A PEG10 H-score cutoff of 35 resulted in a sensitivity of 78.1% and specificity of 90.0% for presence of a DICER1 'hotspot' mutation. PEG10 is a biomarker that is elevated in many DRTP tumors from both sexes bearing a variety of DICER1 'hotspot' variants. PEG10 may act as a cancer-placental antigen/cancer-testis antigen, whose expression could create a possible target for cancer immunotherapies. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: The association between time to treatment initiation (TTI) and metastatic progression in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the association between TTI and subsequent metastasis among patients undergoing curative-intent resection for PDAC. Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries aged ≥ 66 years with nonmetastatic PDAC who underwent curative-intent resection from 2017 to 2021 were identified. TTI was defined as the interval from diagnosis to first cancer-directed treatment and modeled continuously per 30-day increase. Three-year metastatic progression was evaluated using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, with death before metastasis as a competing event. Each 30-day increase in TTI was independently associated with a 14.2% higher subhazard of metastasis (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.142; 95% CI, 1.119-1.166; p < 0.001). The association persisted across surgery alone (sHR, 1.130), neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery (sHR, 1.187), surgery followed by adjuvant therapy (sHR, 1.144), and trimodality therapy (sHR, 1.125) (all p < 0.001). In sensitivity analysis restricted to TTI ≤ 90 days, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant (sHR, 1.064; 95% CI, 0.964-1.174; p = 0.22). Longer TTI was associated with increased metastatic progression across treatment pathways, although this association was attenuated among patients with TTI ≤ 90 days. Further studies are needed to determine whether treatment timing independently influences metastatic progression.

papers.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) offers survival benefit for select patients with peritoneal surface malignancies (PSMs), yet the ethical dimensions of patient selection, informed consent, and multidisciplinary care remain underexplored. In a field still evolving, where patients with comparable profiles may exhibit vastly different prognoses, a structured ethical framework can serve as a compass for surgical decision-making. A narrative review of the literature examined the ethical considerations surrounding CRS/HIPEC for PSM. Topics include patient selection, the biological spectrum from indolent to aggressive disease, technical feasibility of complete cytoreduction, shared decision-making, surgical morbidity, palliative care integration, and special populations. The strength of evidence supporting CRS/HIPEC varies substantially by tumor biology, from near-curative outcomes in low-grade appendiceal neoplasms to marginal benefit in aggressive histologies such as sarcomatoid mesothelioma and signet ring cell carcinoma. When complete cytoreduction cannot be achieved, the procedure is unlikely to confer meaningful survival benefit and may cause significant harm. Traditional informed consent often omits the elements of informed decision-making; structured frameworks such as Best Case/Worst Case and REMAP (Reframe, Expect emotion, Map values, Align, Propose a plan) can bridge this gap. Decision regret data suggest that inadequate preoperative expectation setting contributes to patient dissatisfaction independent of surgical outcomes. Early palliative care and multidisciplinary collaboration improve prognostic understanding and alignment of treatment with patient goals. The ethical principles presented here are not rigid boundaries but flexible guides to help surgeons navigate clinical uncertainty. Although they focus on the surgical decision, they extend to every member of the multidisciplinary team caring for patients with PSM.

papers.abstract: The optimal extent of lymph node examination in older adults undergoing curative-intent gastric adenocarcinoma treatment remains uncertain, as concerns about postoperative complications and potentially decreased benefit in overall survival may lead surgeons toward more limited dissections. Patients with stage I-III gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent gastrectomy between 2010 and 2022 were identified using the National Cancer Database. Patients were stratified by age ( 75th percentile length of stay) were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses were performed in patients aged ≥ 80 and ≥ 85 years. Among the 47,342 patients identified, 11,235 were aged ≥ 75 years. Examination of ≥ 35 lymph nodes compared with < 16 nodes was associated with improved survival in patients aged < 55 years (hazard ratio [HR] 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.87), 55-64 years (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.57-0.77), 65-74 years (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.58-0.76), and ≥ 75 years (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.61-0.91). This was persistent among patients who received preoperative chemotherapy and patients aged ≥ 80 years. Greater nodal yield was not associated with higher odds of adverse modified textbook short-term outcomes in any age group. Greater nodal yield was associated with improved survival and equivalent or improved short-term outcomes across all age groups, even in older patients. These findings suggest age alone should not justify limiting lymphadenectomy in resectable gastric adenocarcinoma.

papers.abstract: Bone and soft tissue sarcomas are heterogeneous cancers. We developed a large language model (LLM)-based extraction workflow to extract six variables from surgical pathology reports of patients with musculoskeletal sarcoma: tumor diagnosis, greatest dimension, closest margin, tumor grade, necrosis, and viability. We hypothesized that the pipeline could achieve clinically acceptable accuracy and serve as a scalable solution to augment or replace manual chart abstraction in sarcoma registry development. We retrospectively collected 1106 surgical pathology notes of patients who underwent surgical resection of bone or soft tissue sarcoma at three sites of a single institution. Notes were split into a training set (n = 353) and a testing set (n = 753). Prompt engineering and fine-tuning were used to query the open-source LLMs Llama3-70B-Instruct and Gemma4-31B-Instruct. Accuracy, F1 score, and specificity were calculated to evaluate the performance of extracted points. On the testing set, both models achieved accuracy of at least 0.85 on extracting all data points and specificity of at least 0.84 on predicting "unknown" when data were not available in the note. The Gemma model achieved higher sensitivity on detecting positive margins than the Llama model: 0.92 versus 0.78. Both LLMs took less than 1 second on average to extract each data point from each pathology note. Registry development for heterogeneous cancers such as sarcoma is limited by the labor-intensive nature of manual data abstraction, and our pipelines achieved promising results. These findings support the feasibility of LLM-based workflows as scalable and accurate alternatives to manual data abstraction for sarcoma clinical registries.

papers.abstract: White matter invasion underlies the lethality of diffuse glioblastoma (GBM), yet its microenvironmental drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we demonstrate that tumor-oligodendrocyte (OL) crosstalk actively promote white matter-associated glioma expansion. In the primary GBM or white matter-invasive glioma, OL lineage cells accumulate at tumor borders and enhance glioma proliferation and migration via secreted factors. Proteomic analysis combined with RNA sequencing identifies OL-derived TMSB4X (thymosin β-4) activates AKT signaling to sustain tumor expansion and invasion. Furthermore, glioma-derived TGF-β stimulates OL differentiation and TMSB4X production, establishing a feed-forward circuit that reinforces tumor progression. Critically, genetic or pharmacological blockade in tumor-OL interaction attenuates glioma outspreading along the white matter in vivo. These findings redefine the OLs as pro-invasive modulators and suggest OL-glioma crosstalk as a therapeutic target in diffuse GBM. Glioblastoma spreads through the brain's white matter while hijacking nearby oligodendrocytes. These cells release TMSB4X, which activates AKT signaling in tumor cells and promotes growth and invasion. In turn, tumors secrete TGF-β, which stimulates oligodendrocytes to produce more TMSB4X. This feed-forward loop may offer a new therapeutic target to prevent glioma from invading the white matter after surgical resection.

papers.abstract: Cardia gastric adenocarcinoma (CGA) is an aggressive malignancy with rising incidence and poor prognosis, driven in part by significant molecular heterogeneity. Through integrated bioinformatics and clinical analyses, we identify Latent-Transforming Growth Factor Beta-Binding Protein 2 (LTBP2) as a key heterogeneously expressed protein markedly upregulated in CGA compared to non-cardia gastric adenocarcinoma (NCGA), correlating with advanced tumor stage and reduced survival. Mechanistically, we uncover a novel post-translational regulation of LTBP2 wherein SIRT1-mediated deacetylation stabilizes LTBP2 by attenuating its binding to the CUL3/SPOP E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby reducing ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Functionally, stabilized LTBP2 activates the TGF-β/PI3K-AKT signaling axis, promoting tumor cell proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and metastasis in vitro and in vivo. Genetic ablation of LTBP2 or SIRT1 impairs tumor growth and EMT, phenotypes rescued by LTBP2 reconstitution. Importantly, LTBP2 deficiency sensitizes tumors to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) chemotherapy, both in cell models and murine xenografts. Collectively, our findings delineate a SIRT1-LTBP2-TGF-β regulatory axis critical for CGA progression and chemoresistance, nominating LTBP2 as a promising therapeutic target in this aggressive gastric cancer subtype.

papers.abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, colocalization and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to contextualize genome-wide association study loci, yet the impact of upstream RNA-sequencing processing choices on these analyses remains critically unexplored. Two poorly characterized decisions include the transcriptomic reference annotation used for quantification of short-read RNA-sequencing samples, which defines transcript composition and structure, and the quantification method itself. Here, through a comprehensive analysis spanning 48 tissues in GTEx and 7 widely studied and diverse phenotypes, we find that these choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction with significant downstream impacts on colocalization and TWAS results. Concordant results across pipelines are further enriched for longer genes, genes with more isoforms, and greater expression heritability. Our findings demonstrate that seemingly minor methodological decisions substantially affect these common analyses, highlighting the need for standardized practices to ensure reproducible genetic association studies.

papers.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal-fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R+ erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4+CSF1R- Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4+ nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal-fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

papers.abstract: Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban-rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. Genetic diversity responded idiosyncratically to urbanisation, with two species showing no detectable urban-rural differences and one species exhibiting reduced diversity in cities, consistent with species-specific ecological traits and habitat requirements. Despite weak population structure and high gene flow in all species, we detected consistent and replicated genomic divergence associated with urban environments. Genome-environment association analyses revealed parallel allele-frequency shifts at the same loci across independent cities for each species, while selective sweep scans identified repeated signals of positive selection in urban populations. Across species, urban-associated divergence was highly polygenic and occurred predominantly in non-coding regions with potential regulatory roles. Although the specific genes involved were largely species-specific, functional enrichment analyses revealed strong convergence across species, particularly in pathways related to physiological stress responses, neurocognitive and behavioural processes, metabolism and immunity. Together, these results suggest that urban environments can impose recurrent selective pressures, generating predictable and parallel genomic responses across cities and species despite ongoing gene flow. More broadly, our findings highlight polygenic, potentially regulatory adaptation as an important component of evolutionary responses to urban environments.

papers.abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion', before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

papers.abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) are strongly influenced by culture medium. We compared OncoPro™ (OP) Tumoroid Culture medium with conventional Wnt/R-spondin/noggin (Wnt) medium. This recently developed OP medium offers a standardized, serum-free alternative to Wnt-based formulations. We compared OP and Wnt media across 36 PDTO lines from various malignancies (colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, biliary head and neck and unknown primary), assessing establishment success. Selected PDTO models were subjected to downstream characterization, including morphological assessment and bulk transcriptomic profiling with comparison to public single-cell RNA sequencing reference datasets (n = 11), whole-exome sequencing (WES) (n = 9), and pharmacological response profiling to a 33-drug panel (n = 3). Adaptation from Wnt medium to OP succeeded in 83.3% (15/18), whereas de novo establishment favored Wnt (33.3% vs 11.1%). Key oncogenic driver alterations were retained across matched organoid cultures, supporting preservation of tumor-relevant genomic features. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed preserved tumor-identity across media, while revealing different epithelial state programs: Wnt upregulated proliferation/stemness-associated genes (e.g. LGR5) and OP enriched adhesion-associated genes and inflammatory/TGF-β programs. In scRNA databases OP signatures preferentially mapped to malignant epithelial compartments in pancreatic cancer, whereas Wnt signatures were linked to non-malignant epithelium. Similarly, in colon cancer OP signature mapped predominantly to the malignant epithelial compartments. Drug (n = 33) screening in pancreatic- and colorectal cancer PDTOs (n = 3) demonstrated consistent medium-dependent shifts: Wnt-grown PDTOs were globally more sensitive in the screened subset, particularly to MAPK-axis inhibitors and apoptosis-sensitizers, while OP-grown PDTOs exhibited relative resistance. Culture medium composition is a key determinant of PDTO phenotype, transcriptome and drug sensitivity. Wnt medium was associated with drug-sensitive states, whereas OP medium was associated with adhesion- and inflammatory-related programs, relative resistance in the screened subset of 33 drugs and closer alignment with malignant epithelial programs in the analyzed pancreatic / colorectal cancer single-cell atlases.

papers.abstract: The development of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) has markedly improved outcomes in Philadelphia chromosome-positive leukemias; however, resistance mediated by BCR::ABL1 kinase domain (KD) mutations remains a major challenge. While the third-generation TKIs ponatinib and asciminib can suppress many resistant mutations including the gatekeeper mutation T315I, their use may be limited by vascular toxicity and emerging resistance, respectively. Compound mutations (CMs), particularly those involving T315I, are frequent in advanced chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia and are largely refractory to approved TKIs when used as monotherapy. Vamotinib (formerly PF-114), a structural analogue of ponatinib with a narrower kinase inhibition profile avoiding vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) inhibition, was developed to retain broad anti-BCR::ABL1 activity while reducing toxicity. Here, we evaluated the in vitro activity of vamotinib against a comprehensive panel of BCR::ABL1 KD mutants using drug concentrations corresponding to clinically relevant dosing regimens and compared the results with available clinical data from a phase-1 trial. Our findings indicate that, even at effective average plasma concentrations corresponding to the maximum tolerated dose, vamotinib exhibits a resistance profile comparable to that of a well-performing second-generation TKI. Notably, high-level resistance persisted for T315I and several P-loop mutations. Clinical responses in mutation-positive patients were largely concordant with these observations. Collectively, these data suggest that vamotinib may not meet the criteria for classification as a third-generation TKI but could have utility in selected patient populations or in rational combination strategies.

papers.abstract: The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. Here we introduce continuous mass photometry, enabling hour-long, mass-resolved observation of individual biomolecules tethered to supported lipid bilayers, their complexes and interactions, with up to sub-kilodalton mass precision and millisecond temporal resolution. Our approach represents a quantitative time-resolved single-molecule measurement modality for studying complex biomolecular mechanisms in action.

papers.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro-myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

papers.abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

papers.abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

papers.abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude - a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

papers.abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam's potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism-associated immune suppression remains a major barrier to durable therapeutic responses. Indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 has been pursued as a therapeutic target, but incomplete pathway suppression has limited clinical success. As the aryl hydrocarbon receptor is a ligand-activated transcription factor and downstream effector of tryptophan metabolism, we investigated how myeloid-cell aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling shapes the tumor immune microenvironment and whether its inhibition can restore antitumor immunity. Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor knockout mice targeting dendritic cells or macrophages were used to evaluate the effects of genetic aryl hydrocarbon receptor ablation. Pharmacologic inhibition was assessed using DA-4505 across syngeneic lung, colorectal, and breast cancer models and an immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory humanized patient-derived xenograft model. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated alone or in combination with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy, chemotherapy, or surgery. Tumor growth, survival, metastasis, and immune remodeling were analyzed by flow cytometry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, cytokine profiling, and human tumor datasets. Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor depletion in macrophages and dendritic cells enhanced innate and adaptive immune activation, increased interferon-γ-producing T cells, and strengthened antitumor immunity. In mouse tumor models, pharmacologic aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade enhanced macrophage chemotaxis and activation programs, promoted M1-like macrophage polarization, increased interferon-γ-producing CD8⁺ T cells, and reduced regulatory T cells and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells. These changes promoted robust T-cell activation and durable tumor control. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition further synergized with chemotherapy, surgery, and immune checkpoint blockade, leading to expansion of effector and memory T-cell populations and sustained antitumor responses. In a humanized lung cancer model, aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade increased intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and cytotoxic-memory programs while reducing regulatory T-cell enrichment. In human tumor datasets, aryl hydrocarbon receptor-positive macrophages correlated with FOXP3⁺ T-cell infiltration, and higher aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition-associated T-cell signatures were associated with improved patient survival.

papers.abstract: Adenosine 5'-monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a highly conserved energy-sensing kinase, plays a central role in maintaining cellular metabolic homeostasis, such as glucose/lipid metabolism, mitochondrial biogenesis, and autophagy, to counteract energetic stress. Beyond the canonical adenylate-dependent activation of AMPK by sensing the ATP:AMP/ADP ratio, emerging evidence reveals noncanonical activation mechanisms. Proper AMPK signaling is essential for physiological functions, whereas its dysregulation underlies various pathologies, including metabolic diseases, immune disorders, and cancer. This review systematically recapitulates the historical background and landmark discoveries of the AMPK field, including the discovery of AMPK, the structure of AMPK complex, upstream regulators and downstream substrates, and the transcriptional/posttranscriptional and posttranslational regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, we delineate its roles in maintaining metabolic equilibrium, mitochondrial integrity, and immune competence across organ systems and highlight how dysregulated AMPK activity contributes to pathological diseases, encompassing alterations in its expression levels, intrinsic kinase activity, subcellular localization or upstream regulatory signaling cascades. Specifically, we focus on knock-in or knockout mouse models utilized to study AMPK-associated human diseases and the translational potential of AMPK-targeting agonists or antagonists across diverse pathological conditions. A deep understanding of the multidimensional regulatory network of AMPK and mechanistic insights with therapeutic innovations that we provide with this review will help address the challenges of complex metabolic diseases.

papers.abstract: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 .

papers.abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: National cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system. We identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded. We developed an analytical framework of 12 elements and 76 sub-elements, aligned with WHO, International Cancer Control Partnership, and Union for International Cancer Control guidance and validated it through a modified two-stage Delphi process (online survey of 67 experts; triangulation workshop with 31 participants). PRISM comprised document ingestion (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), policy analysis with retrieval-augmented generation (Llama 4 Scout, 109B), and semantic quality assurance. PRISM was validated against masked dual-expert ratings for six purposely selected NCCPs, then applied to all NCCPs. Scores were normalised to 0-5 and medians compared across World Bank income group and WHO region. We identified 50 NCCPs that met the inclusion criteria. Median overall comprehensiveness was 2·78 (IQR 2·25-3·09), with high comprehensiveness classified as 4·0-5·0, moderate as 2·0-3·9, and low as 0-1·9. Europe (2·96; 2·78-3·35) and lower-middle-income countries (2·97; 2·48-3·15) had the highest medians; the western Pacific (2·21; 1·78-2·87) and low-income countries (2·05; 1·94-2·22) had the lowest. Element-level medians were highest for implementation (4·17; 3·54-4·38), health services (3·89; 2·63-4·19), and governance and organisation (3·67; 3·35-3·98), and lowest for financing (1·88; 1·00-2·69), outcomes (1·83; 1·33-2·33), and threats (2·19; 1·72-2·34). Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less. Our analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data. Harvard University.

papers.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.

papers.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

papers.abstract: Chicago has a high degree of care fragmentation, with multiple large health systems and numerous safety-net systems. Fragmentation may be why the west and south areas of Chicago have high incidences of cervical cancer despite high self-reported screening rates. This study assesses utilization of cervical cancer screening-associated tests and procedures across seven health systems in Chicago between 2012 and 2022. This retrospective cohort study included females aged 15+ years enrolled in one or more health systems in the CAPriCORN network. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, geolocation, linear mixed-effects model, and Poisson regression. Proportions and trends in utilization by year of test modalities (cytology alone, cytology and human papillomavirus (HPV) test [cotest], HPV test alone, colposcopy, and cervical procedures [cone biopsy, loop electrosurgical excision procedure, and ablation]) were calculated and stratified by Chicago's six geographic zones. The time between screening utilization was compared by age, Chicago zone, and change in health system. Of 1.20 million in the study cohort, 53.6% had only 1 screening test during the 11-year study period; 22.9% had 2 tests, and 22.9% had 3 or more. Individuals in Chicago who changed health systems between two consecutive screening tests had a longer median interval between tests compared with those who did not change (34 versus 15.4 months). Over half of the cohort only had one screening test and may be underscreened. Switching health systems more than doubled the time interval between screening tests compared with patients who remained in the same system.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options and a high risk of relapse and mortality. Consequently, there is a critical need for personalized treatment strategies that reflect the unique biology, clonal architecture, and evolutionary dynamics of individual tumors. Here, we present a TNBC digital twin framework, built from prior knowledge and formulated as a mechanistic qualitative network in which nodes represent genes and proteins and edges denote the interactions between them. Parameterized with patient-specific molecular data, the model identifies potential resistance mechanisms and proposes tailored treatment plans to overcome them. We validate the model using clinical data from PARTNER, a large, randomized controlled trial evaluating platinum-based chemotherapy with or without PARP inhibitors. The model accurately predicts treatment responses and identifies mutational and transcriptional biomarkers associated with clinical outcome. Our approach offers an interpretable alternative to black-box predictive models, enabling transparent decision-making in precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are driving a major shift in modern medicine, particularly within radiation oncology. AI in radiation oncology offers low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) a way to offset critical shortages of oncologists and physicists by automating segmentation, planning, and quality checks, improving efficiency, and expanding equitable access to care. Its actual value depends on validation against LMICs' infrastructure and patient populations, an area where current evidence remains limited. This review aims to comprehensively summarize the current evidence on AI and ML applications across key domains of radiotherapy, while highlighting global disparities in adoption, particularly in LMICs. This critical review conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2010 and April 2026. Only relevant studies emphasizing the efficiency of AI in radiation workflow and the existing gaps in its adoption within LMICs were included in this review. Eleven studies published between 2019 and 2025 were included. Study designs comprised original research (n=5), reviews (n=4), a survey (n=1), and a study protocol (n=1). Studies were conducted across multiple LMICs in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, predominantly evaluating AI-based contouring and treatment-planning tools, with Radiation Planning Assistant (RPA) being the most frequently reported platform. AI tools demonstrated comparable performance in LMICs relative to High-Income Countries (HICs), particularly with regard to time efficiency and the quality of target volume contouring. Yet the majority of LMICs still don't have AI tools in their radiation centers to work efficiently. The current literature reveals a gap between the need for AI in radiation oncology in LMICs and the available evidence supporting its implementation. LMICs could benefit substantially from AI-enabled improvements in radiation oncology. Several conclusions about the applicability of these findings in LMIC settings were drawn by extrapolation from studies conducted in HIC contexts, which substantially limits their direct generalizability to lower-resource environments. Cost-effective and accessible AI models hold promise to address workforce shortages, improve efficiency, and expand equitable access to quality radiotherapy services.

papers.abstract: With the rising prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), preventing new-onset disease becomes a priority. The PIONIR (Preventing IBD ONset in Individuals at Risk) randomized controlled trial explored whether the Tasty&Healthy (T&H) diet reduces inflammatory markers in high-risk first-degree relatives (FDRs) of patients with Crohn's disease (CD). FDRs with persistently elevated fecal calprotectin (FC, >70μg/g) and, at most, nonspecific mucosal abnormalities (edema or ≤10 aphthous ulcers) on video-capsule endoscopy or ileocolonoscopy were randomized to T&H or habitual diet (HD) for 8 weeks, followed by crossover for additional 8 weeks. Treatment effect on the primary outcome, FC response, was analyzed using generalized estimating equations for the two-period, two-sequence crossover design, following the intention-to-treat principle. Twenty-nine FDRs were randomized (n=14 T&H-first, n=15 HD-first). At week 8, median FC was lower with T&H (64μg/g [IQR 44-127]) vs. HD (112μg/g [74-227]; P=.022). FC decreased by ≥50% in 71% on T&H versus 27% on HD (RR=2.68 [95%CI 1.09-6.60]; P=.016). Across both crossover periods, estimated marginal mean FC declined from 185μg/g [95%CI 144-237] by 61% to 72μg/g [95%CI 57-91] with T&H, versus 38% to 114μg/g [95%CI 93-140] with HD (ratio 0.63 [95%CI 0.51-0.80], translating to 37% overall decrease with T&H; P<0.001). Six microbial species differed between diets after FDR correction. By week 8, 79% rated T&H acceptable and 83% had good or complete adherence. These findings demonstrate the modifiability of low-grade intestinal inflammation in healthy high-risk FDRs with persistent FC elevation but without diagnostic endoscopic evidence of CD, supporting long-term dietary prevention trials (ClinicalTrials.gov #NCT05211518).

papers.abstract: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines. Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026. Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis. The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) extensive genomic heterogeneity and immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) are major factors contributing to treatment resistance. This study aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which Robustic Acid 4-O-amino substituted synthetic derivatives (MF1), a novel robustic acid derivative, derived from structural modifications of natural products from Dalbergia benthamii Prain, targets carcinogenic signaling and synergistically regulates the crosstalk between autophagy and ferroptosis to induce programmed cell death in HCC. In vitro functional assays confirmed that MF1 exhibits significant antitumor activity. Mechanistically, MF1 significantly upregulates cellular oxidative stress levels, inducing characteristic changes in mitochondrial ultrastructure and apoptosis; simultaneously, by promoting intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation and downregulating the expression of key ferroptosis regulators GPX4 and SLC7A11, it potently activates the ferroptosis process. Concurrently, MF1 continuously activates the cytotoxic autophagy pathway by regulating the LC3 I/II conversion ratio and upregulating the expression of core autophagy proteins ATG5 and Beclin-1. Network pharmacology identified 7 core targets of MF1 that are common to both ferroptosis and autophagy regulation. qPCR validation showed that MF1 significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of these 7 core oncogenes in HepG2 cells. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities between MF1 and five core targets, 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations further validated the conformational stability of all five top-ranked MF1-protein complexes, with the higher binding stability for AKT1, SRC and MTOR. In summary, this study clarifies MF1 induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in HepG2 cells, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic option for HCC.

papers.abstract: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866). Between Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; p<0·0001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63 (83%) of 76 with zamto-cel and in 65 (86%) of 76 with R-GemOx. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (28 [37%] with zamto-cel and 17 [22%] with R-GemOx), anaemia (11 [14%] and 12 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (20 [26%] and seven [9%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 31 (41%) patients with zamto-cel and 50 (66%) with R-GemOx, most commonly malignant neoplasm progression (11 [14%] and 38 [50%]), cytokine release syndrome (CRS; six [8%] and none), and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (four [5%] and none). Treatment-related deaths occurred in two (3%) of 82 patients with zamto-cel (due to CRS and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and in one (1%) of 78 with R-GemOx (malignant lymphoma progression). The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation. Miltenyi Biomedicine.

papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) drives intestinal barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, and liver injury, yet the epithelial mechanisms remain undefined. Autophagy and lysosomes maintain intestinal epithelial homoeostasis and barrier integrity, but their response to chronic alcohol exposure is unclear. Human intestinal tissues from individuals with and without AUD were analysed alongside human intestinal organoids. Wild-type, CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3, GFP-LC3B, and Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice underwent chronic-binge ethanol feeding. Organoids and Caco-2 cells were exposed to ethanol (50 mM) with or without bafilomycin A1 or Torin-2. Autophagy-lysosome pathways were assessed using transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, biochemical fractionation, and flux reporters. Alcohol induced heterogeneous autophagy-lysosome responses characterised by lysosomal stress/adaptive remodelling. These changes occurred with limited autophagosome formation and maturation, resulting in impaired autophagic throughput. These responses differed along the crypt-villus axis and between intestinal regions. Disrupted autophagy was associated with altered trafficking and accumulation of claudin-2. Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice exhibited increased baseline intestinal permeability vs wild-type controls (p = 0.03). Following ethanol exposure, Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice showed greater intestinal permeability (p = 0.003), circulating and hepatic endotoxin (p = 0.002), hepatic triglycerides (p = 0.01), and serum ALT (p = 0.02) vs ethanol-fed wild-type mice. Alcohol disrupts intestinal autophagy-lysosome homoeostasis in a spatially heterogeneous manner, accompanied by defective epithelial proteostasis and tight junction dysregulation. Impaired autophagosome formation exacerbates gut permeability and liver injury, supporting intestinal autophagy as a potential therapeutic target in alcohol-associated disease. Broader applicability of the human findings requires validation in larger cohorts. This study was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

papers.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

papers.abstract: This phase 2 trial included 211 Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (mean age 48.4 years; 131 participants were male). Participants received once-weekly subcutaneous UBT251 (2 mg, 4 mg [initial dose 0.5 mg], 4 mg [initial dose 1 mg], or 6 mg), 1 mg semaglutide, or placebo for 24 weeks. At week 24, UBT251 achieved least-squares mean changes in glycated hemoglobin of -2.16% (95% CI, -2.39 to -1.92) to -1.98% (95% CI, -2.31 to -1.64), versus -1.77% (95% CI, -1.99 to -1.54) for semaglutide and -0.66% (95% CI, -0.90 to -0.41) for placebo (placebo-adjusted differences: -1.50% to -1.32%; all p < 0.001). UBT251 significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, 2-h postprandial glucose, and waist circumference versus placebo (all p < 0.001). Weight reduction with UBT251 was significantly greater than both placebo and semaglutide (all p < 0.05). Gastrointestinal events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events. These findings support further phase 3 evaluation of UBT251. Registration: CTR20250029; NCT07163624.

papers.abstract: Whether intestinal fungal dysbiosis contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. We investigated how gut Candida albicans influences HCC progression, immune remodeling, and response to ICI therapy. Fecal and tumor samples from patients with HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls were analyzed using ITS2 sequencing, immune profiling, and correlation analyses. Mechanistic studies focused on four complementary autochthonous murine HCC models and cell-based assays, integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, genetic and pharmacologic perturbations, Kaede photoconversion, fungal antigen recall assays, antifungal treatment, and anti-PD-1 therapy. Fecal C. albicans abundance was higher in HCC patients and was associated with advanced disease, shorter overall survival, and reduced durable clinical benefit. Across HCC models, C. albicans gavage increased tumor burden and induced a Th17/IL-17A-skewed microenvironment characterized by Trem2+ macrophage accumulation and impaired CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Antifungal treatment attenuated tumor progression, whereas IL-17A blockade or deficiency largely abrogated C. albicans-associated tumor promotion. Mechanistically, IL-17A induced tumor-derived MCP-1 through ACT1-TRAF6-TAK1 signaling to recruit macrophages and upregulated PAI-1, which activated TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to promote an immunosuppressive Trem2+ macrophage state. These macrophages limited CD8+ T cell recruitment and effector function through coordinated CXCL10 repression and GAL-1 induction, while potentially reinforcing Th17 responses through IL-1β and IL-6. Kaede photoconversion demonstrated enhanced mesenteric lymph node-to-liver Th17 trafficking, while fungal antigen recall assays revealed preferential Th17 responsiveness to C. albicans. C. albicans also impaired anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo, whereas antifungal treatment partially restored therapeutic responsiveness. Intestinal C. albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance through an IL-17A-Trem2+ macrophage circuit, supporting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target. Intestinal fungal dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a component of the gut-liver axis, but its functional contribution to HCC has remained poorly defined. Our study identifies intestinal Candida albicans as a promoter of HCC progression in experimental models and delineates an IL-17A-MCP-1/PAI-1-Trem2+ macrophage circuit that links fungal exposure to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity and reduced response to PD-1 blockade. These findings are relevant to researchers and clinicians seeking microbiome-associated determinants of HCC progression and immunotherapy resistance. Fecal C. albicans abundance and components of this immune circuit may warrant evaluation as biomarkers for patient stratification and as potential targets for combination therapy. However, the clinical associations reported here are based on modest observational cohorts, and antifungal treatment was tested as a proof-of-concept intervention in mice. Larger prospective studies and more selective therapeutic approaches will therefore be required before these findings can inform clinical management.

papers.abstract: Mucin-16 (MUC16) is overexpressed in >60% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and correlates with poor outcomes, yet its role in regulating tumor-immune interactions remains incompletely defined. Using KPC and KPC-MUC16 knockout (KPC-MUC16KO) genetically engineered and orthotopic mouse models, we show that loss of MUC16 markedly reduces tumor burden and reprograms the tumor microenvironment (TME) toward a less immunosuppressive state. MUC16 deficiency significantly decreased CD206+ and Ym1/2+ M2-like macrophages, increased the M1/M2 ratio, and improved survival. Cytokine profiling identified CCL2 and Serpin-E1 as MUC16- dependent secreted factors that promote macrophage recruitment and polarization; neutralization of these cytokines reduced macrophage migration in vitro. Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) exposed to MUC16-expressing tumor cells or conditioned media adopted a CD206+Arg1+ M2-like phenotype, whereas MUC16KO tumor signals favored inflammatory CD86+iNOS+ M1-like polarization. Macrophage depletion using clodronate liposomes significantly impaired tumor growth in MUC16-competent tumors but had minimal effect in KPC-MUC16KO tumors, indicating dependence on macrophage-mediated immunosuppression in the former group. Spatial transcriptomics revealed a globally distinct TME in MUC16KO tumors, including enhanced antigen-presentation programs, increased complement activation, and fibroblast states skewed toward pro-inflammatory signaling. These findings establish MUC16 as a key orchestrator of macrophage-driven immunosuppression in PDAC and support therapeutic strategies combining MUC16-targeted interventions with TME-reprogramming approaches.

papers.abstract: The role of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) remains controversial, mainly because of the lack of high-level evidence. We aim to update the evidence on NAC regarding pathological and oncological outcomes in patients with nonmetastatic UTUC. Moreover, we also aimed to give an overview of neoadjuvant immunotherapy (NAI) in the current clinical scenario. A systematic review of 41 studies on NAC and NAI (eight prospective studies [PS] or randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 33 retrospective studies [RS]) was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Outcomes of interest included pathological complete response (pCR), pathological partial response (pPR), pathological downstaging, overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), and disease-free survival (DFS). Pooled analyses were performed using effect sizes for pathological outcomes and hazard ratios (HRs) for survival outcomes. Finally, 5-yr proportions were summarized when a 5-yr time threshold was available. Of the 41 articles, 30 (five PS or RCTs and 25 RS) were eligible for meta-analysis (n = 2384 patients). The pooled pCR, pPR, and pathological downstaging rates were, respectively, 11% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10-12), 44% (95% CI: 38-50), and 20% (95% CI: 10-37). Compared with radical nephroureterectomy (RNU), NAC was associated with pooled HRs of 0.56 (95% CI: 0.39-0.80) for OS, 0.47 (95% CI: 0.26-0.85) for CSS, and 0.55 (95% CI: 0.24-1.26) for DFS. Evidence on NAI remains limited in terms of sample size and is primarily derived from early-phase studies. NAC was associated with favorable oncological outcomes compared with RNU alone. Nevertheless, the absence of prospective randomized studies limits the strength of the evidence, and further high-quality trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Subsets of intestinal CD4+ T cells directly recognize commensal bacteria and coordinate tolerance versus protective immunity. Our limited understanding of CD4+ T cell specificities and corresponding functional phenotypes has created a barrier to deciphering the mechanisms of mucosal homeostasis and inflammation mediated by the adaptive immune system. To address this, we leveraged an immunodominant Bacteroidetes epitope in SusC to perform single-cell profiling of the SusC-specific and total CD4+ T cell landscapes in intestinal tissues of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). By analyzing phenotypes and T cell receptor specificities in parallel, we uncovered phenotypic diversification of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in IBD and identified an epithelial-localized, SusC-reactive Th17 subset that is BACH2lo, GZMAhi, and expresses the costimulatory receptor TMIGD2. Together, our results highlight the utility of tracking commensal-specific T cell responses to define specialized subsets of Th17 cells associated with loss of tolerance to the microbiome.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains one of the most common serious complications after noncardiac surgery, and intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is consistently identified as a modifiable risk factor. Observational studies show a consistent, roughly dose-response association between IOH, particularly at mean arterial pressures below 60-65 mmHg, and postoperative AKI, with stronger associations in patients with limited renal reserve. Definitions of IOH vary widely, which complicates the comparison of studies and the translation of thresholds into clinical targets. Randomized trials of individualized or higher blood pressure targets have generally not confirmed a kidney-protective benefit, and pooled analyses with trial sequential analysis have not demonstrated that higher targets reduce AKI. This narrative review examines how IOH definitions evolved, summarizes the conflicting intervention evidence, and assesses the controversies that shape current practice. The review concludes that avoiding severe and sustained hypotension remains reasonable, whereas current randomized trial evidence does not support a general kidney-protective benefit of higher or individualized blood pressure targets. This conclusion is provisional and is tempered by the methodologic and causal uncertainties.

papers.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

papers.abstract: To prospectively explore efficacy and safety of radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy for locoregional recurrent cervical cancer (CC). Patients with locoregional recurrent CC were enrolled in the analysis. The enrolled patients received radiotherapy and albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety. 99 patients were enrolled. For all patients, the 3-year PFS and 3-year OS were 48.5% and 58.6%. 17.2% of patients achieved CR and 67.7% of patients achieved PR. The ORR was 84.8%. Moreover, 10.1% of patients were confirmed SD. The DCR was 94.9%. Locoregional recurrent CC could benefit from radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy.
